addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - API usage, tool use, Anthropic SDK usage. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- qemu-runner: Use this agent when you need to run a RISC-V ELF binary through Andes QEMU and get its output. Always use this agent instead of running QEMU directly, as it handles the semihosting fd 9 output capture quirk in Claude Code's sandbox.

Examples:

- assistant: *builds a test binary*
  assistant: "Let me use the qemu-runner agent to execute the binary and check the output"

- user: "Run this ELF at VLEN=512"
  assistant: "I'll use the qemu-runner agent to run it" (Tools: Bash, Read) (Tools: Bash)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

- cc-log: Lightweight system log to record all Claude Code behavior (tool use, subagent creation, compaction, permissions, session lifecycle) for analysis. Use when the user wants to enable/disable behavior logging, analyze Claude Code session logs, list saved logs, or understand Claude Code's tool usage patterns. Trigger on: "cc-log", "behavior log", "system log", "record behavior", "log enable", "log disable", "analyze log".
- iree-optimizer: Agentic per-dispatch tile-size tuner for IREE CPU codegen on RISC-V. Keeps IREE's chosen pipeline (CPUDoubleTilingExpert / CPUConvTileAndDecomposeExpert / CPUBufferOpsTileAndVectorize) and only overrides the root linalg op's lowering_config<tile_sizes = [...]>. Each round reads the best-so-far RISC-V assembly (LMUL, VLmax, register spills) to ground the next tile-size proposal; pre-compile divisibility gate ensures tiles divide their parent extents (no tail loop); a post-compile check of the IR after iree-codegen-generic-vectorization confirms no tail/masked main path. Compiles via iree_tuner.py, benchmarks on FPGA, iterates. Use whenever the user mentions tuning IREE dispatch tile sizes, agentic tile search, or wants to replace GA-based tile-size search with LLM-driven search. Trigger on "iree optimize", "optimize dispatch", "tile tune", or references to dispatch .mlir files for performance tuning.
- libnn-optimizer: Autonomous optimization workflow for libnn RISC-V neural network library functions
in the agentic_libnn_opt project. Use this skill when the user wants to optimize a
libnn function for FPGA performance, run the libnn optimization loop, validate the
optimization config, parse FPGA hardware features, extract shapes from perf test files,
or manage the optimization state machine. Trigger when: user mentions "optimize",
"libnn", "FPGA perf", "optimization loop", "validate config",
"phase gather/baseline/iterate/evaluate", "perf test", or references opt/config.toml,
opt/state.json, or any libnn function optimization task.
- libnn-wiki-writer: Internal style guide for writing docs/wiki/ pages during /libnn-optimizer learn phase. Not a standalone skill -- read by the optimize agent.
- mlir-transform-writer: Write MLIR transform dialect scripts that directly control IR lowering - tiling, fusion, vectorization, bufferization, GPU thread mapping, shared memory promotion, and more. Use this skill whenever someone asks to generate, write, or modify a transform dialect script, transform library, codegen strategy, or tuning spec in MLIR. Also trigger when the request involves composing IR transformations for linalg ops, controlling IREE codegen pipelines via transform dialect, or replacing annotation-only configs with full transform strategies. Covers both upstream MLIR transform ops and IREE-specific extensions.
- skill-creator: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.
- spec-human: Create a human-reviewable architecture spec using a 6-section template (Summary, Background, Architecture, Interface, Edge Cases, Alternatives) BEFORE implementing a non-trivial design. Triggered explicitly via /spec-human <topic>, or when the user says "write a human spec", "create a review-ready design doc", "spec this out for review", or "I need a spec for X before we build it". Produces an ASCII markdown document at ./specs/<slug>.md aimed at peer engineers and tech leads who need to validate core architecture and trade-offs in 5 minutes. Do NOT auto-trigger on general design questions or coding tasks - this is a deliberate review gate that only fires on explicit request. For LLM-targeted specs (future sibling skill), use /spec-llm instead.
- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- ralph-loop:cancel-ralph: Cancel active Ralph Loop
- ralph-loop:help: Explain Ralph Loop plugin and available commands
- ralph-loop:ralph-loop: Start Ralph Loop in current session
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

1	# andesim-demo test roadmap
2	
3	Each entry is one independent demo. One session builds ONE demo, then flips
4	its State and commits. States: `TODO`, `IN PROGRESS`, `DONE`, `BLOCKED`.
5	
6	Conventions (same as the existing demos):
7	
8	- Layout: `demo/<name>/main.c` + `demo/<name>/Makefile`; host-side checks go
9	  in `demo/<name>/check.sh` (the `memsize` precedent).
10	- Top-level `Makefile` gets `run-<name>` and the per-mode targets; `README.md`
11	  gets a short section describing what the demo proves.
12	- Pass signal: either the guest prints `<NAME>_OK` from inside the ROI, or
13	  `check.sh` asserts on the driver's output. Every demo must fail loudly.
14	- Demos run on every mode where the feature exists (some are hybrid-only or
15	  fast-only; each entry says which).
16	
17	Priority = file order. 1-3 are headline USER_GUIDE features with zero demo
18	coverage today.
19	
20	---
21	
22	## 0. ok-grep: assert the *_OK line on every run target
23	
24	State: TODO
25	Modes: all (harness change, no new guest code).
26	
27	The 2026-07-16 fpga_l3 bring-up proved the "fail loudly" convention has a
28	hole: rvv, fp and syscall print their *_OK from inside the ROI, but their
29	`run` targets only propagate the exit code -- on hybrid the run ends at the
30	exit trigger, so a run whose in-ROI output silently VANISHED still exits 0.
31	That exact failure shipped: a coherence-manager RTL wedge dropped all in-ROI
32	UART output on ax46mpv_fpga_l3 and three demos kept "passing"; only
33	demo/cache had check.sh teeth (vsim_andesim 9be968a fixed the wedge).
34	Deliverable: each demo whose pass signal is a printed marker greps for it in
35	the run target (or gets a small check.sh), so lost output = red sweep.
36	
37	- Key files: demo/{rvv,fp,syscall,lm,lm_slave,hvm_slave,cpp}/Makefile
38	  (or per-demo check.sh), README.md.
39	- Pass: `make check-all-engines` fails if any *_OK line goes missing.
40	- Deps: none.
41	
42	---
43	
44	## 1. hotloops
45	
46	State: DONE
47	Modes: hybrid (pc trigger); the detector itself runs fast.
48	
49	Measure a binary you cannot edit. `main.c` has one known hot loop (a
50	checksum over an array, >=10 iterations) and NO ROI markers. `check.sh`
51	runs `$(ANDESIM)/build/hotloops --min-iters 10 <elf>`, asserts the report
52	names the hot function, extracts the ready `measure:` line (a
53	`--pc-start`/`--pc-end` pair), and pastes it into
54	`./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger pc ...`. Closed loop: the detector's
55	output feeds the measurement command with no human guessing.
56	
57	- Key files: `demo/hotloops/{main.c,Makefile,check.sh}`, top `Makefile`, `README.md`
58	- Pass: check.sh sees the hot function in the hotloops report AND a
59	  `[andesim] N cycles` line from the hybrid run using the reported PCs.
60	- Deps: none. Reference: USER_GUIDE 4.3, docs/hotloops.md.
61	
62	## 2. verify
63	
64	State: DONE
65	Modes: hybrid only (marker trigger).
66	
67	Trust the figure. A state-heavy workload (GPR churn, scalar FP math under
68	RTZ, a strip-mined RVV loop, CSR writes staged before AND inside the ROI)
69	runs with `--verify`: andesim re-runs the ELF on pure QEMU up to the ROI
70	exit and compares the drained state field by field against the cycle
71	engine. Two builds from one source: `verify.elf` must PASS; the teeth are
72	`verify_taint.elf`, identical except one instruction sampling `mcycle`
73	into `t6` at the exit marker -- engine-divergent by design, so verify
74	must FAIL, name exactly `x31`, and exit non-zero. In the sweep the demo
75	is V-gated (`NEED_V`): the kernel uses RVV intrinsics.
76	
77	- Key files: `demo/verify/{main.c,Makefile,check.sh}`, top `Makefile`, `README.md`
78	- Pass: check.sh asserts `[state-diff] PASS` + `[verify] PASS: vsim drain
79	  matches the QEMU oracle` on the clean build, and rc!=0 +
80	  `[state-diff] x31:` + `FAIL: 1 mismatch` on the taint build.
81	- Deps: none. Reference: USER_GUIDE 5.7.
82	
83	## 3. kanata
84	
85	State: TODO
86	Modes: hybrid only.
87	
88	See the pipeline of exactly the ROI. A small kernel runs with
89	`--kanata roi.kanata --objdump kernel.S` (the dump generated at build time
90	with `objdump -d`). Users open the file in Konata; check.sh proves it is
91	well-formed without a GUI.
92	
93	- Key files: `demo/kanata/{main.c,Makefile,check.sh}`, top `Makefile`, `README.md`
94	- Pass: check.sh asserts the Kanata header line, that a known kernel
95	  mnemonic from the objdump is embedded, and the trace is non-trivial
96	  (more than a handful of retired instructions).
97	- Constraint to demo: marker mode needs exactly ONE exit marker in the ELF
98	  (more -> andesim errors and points at `--trigger pc`).
99	- Deps: none. Reference: USER_GUIDE 5.8.
100	
101	## 4. engines
102	
103	State: DONE
104	Modes: the whole suite, once per installed vsim engine.
105	
106	One suite, N cores - design-space switching, not a new demo dir. Every
107	demo's cycle/hybrid target already takes `ENGINE=<id>`, so the deliverable
108	is the sweep: `make check-all-engines` runs the aggregate `check` once per
109	vsim engine parsed from `andesim list engines` at run time (restrict with
110	`SWEEP_ENGINES="vsim:a ..."`) and prints a per-engine OK/FAILED summary.
111	Demos are capability-gated per engine from the driver's own output: the
112	lm*/hvm* demos skip when the engine's resolved hybrid plan (`--dry-run`)
113	carries no ILM/DLM/HVM sidecar args (`ax46mpv_advanced` has none), and rvv
114	skips when the engine's `list engines` row shows no VLEN.
115	
116	- Key files: top `Makefile` (`check-all-engines`), `README.md`
117	- Pass: `make check-all-engines` exits 0. Teeth: a bogus engine in
118	  SWEEP_ENGINES makes the sweep report FAILED and exit nonzero.
119	- Deps: none.
120	
121	## 5. fp
122	
123	State: DONE
124	Modes: fast, cycle, hybrid (marker + pc).
125	
126	Scalar FP state transport - fills the coverage gap next to `rvv` (which is
127	integer-V only). The QEMU phase sets a non-default rounding mode (`frm` =
128	RTZ) and raises a sticky `fflags` bit; the vsim ROI computes a
129	rounding-mode-sensitive result and checks: the result matches
130	expected-for-RTZ, and the pre-ROI sticky flag is still set. Proves
131	`fcsr` (+ `mstatus.FS`) crossed the handoff.
132	
133	- Key files: `demo/fp/{main.c,Makefile}`, top `Makefile`, `README.md`
134	- Pass: guest prints `FP_OK`.
135	- Deps: none.
136	
137	## 6. cache
138	
139	State: DONE
140	Modes: hybrid (marker), two variants of one source.
141	
142	Why timing-config transport matters. The same kernel is built twice from
143	one `main.c`: variant A keeps crt0's cache enable (transported
144	`mcache_ctl`), variant B writes `mcache_ctl = 0` before the ROI. check.sh
145	runs both hybrid measurements and asserts the uncached figure is much
146	larger. Doubles as a write-mask demo: the restore carries variant B's
147	disable only because the program itself wrote the CSR.
148	
149	- Key files: `demo/cache/{main.c,Makefile,check.sh}`, top `Makefile`, `README.md`
150	- Pass: check.sh asserts `cycles(off) > 2 * cycles(on)` (calibrate the
151	  factor once real numbers exist).
152	- Deps: none. Reference: USER_GUIDE section 6 ("Config that matters for
153	  timing rides along").
154	
155	### 6b. cache: L2C/L3C MMIO transport leg
156	
157	State: DONE (2026-07-15)
158	Modes: hybrid only (marker) -- fast never leaves QEMU's stub, cycle never
159	leaves the RTL; only hybrid crosses the boundary under test.
160	
161	Prove the platform shared-cache registers at 0xE0500000 ride the handoff:
162	the QEMU leg stages Control policy bits (RMW), HPM Control 0 and
163	WAYMASK0-4; the vsim ROI reads them back FROM THE RTL and prints
164	`L2C_OK`/`L3C_OK` before the exit marker. Separate tests per cache level
165	(one source, `-DSHC_L3`): the block is the L2C on 45-series engines, the
166	L3C on 46/66. Engine-gated by the `list engines` CACHE column (from
167	`--describe shared_cache_*`, which the vsim gate derives from the RTL's
168	`NDS_L2C/L3C_CACHE_SIZE_KB`). RO registers (Configuration, INITSTATUS)
169	and side-effect registers (CCTL command, W1C error) are excluded by
170	design. Passes on ax66_makatau (live 512K L3C); SKIPs naming the RTL
171	config on ax45mpv_premium/ax46mpv_advanced (built size 0). Companion
172	changes: vsim gate extension + Control policy-bit merge + describe keys;
173	driver descriptor/plan `l2c_base=`/verify mask/CACHE column.
174	
175	- Key files: `demo/cache/{l2c.c,Makefile,check.sh}`, `README.md`;
176	  vsim_andesim `src/hybrid/{shared_cache_config.hpp,resume_driver.hpp}`,
177	  `src/{simulator.hpp,main.cpp}`; andesim
178	  `driver/{engine_descriptor.hpp,run_plan.cpp,state_diff.cpp,cmd_list.cpp}`;
179	  ABI `hybrid/state_abi.h` (`HYBRID_L2C_CTRL_POLICY_MASK`).
180	- Pass: `make check-cache ENGINE=vsim:ax66_makatau` prints
181	  `[PASS] hybrid L3C transport (L3:512K)`; ax45/ax46 print the
182	  RTL-config SKIP.
183	- Deps: none.
184	
185	## 7. roi_rules
186	
187	State: TODO
188	Modes: hybrid (marker + pc) vs cycle as the reference.
189	
190	Trigger semantics and measurement hygiene, executable. A `noinline` kernel
191	is called 3 times; both triggers are one-shot, so the measured window is
192	the FIRST call only. check.sh asserts the hybrid figure is far below the
193	cycle-mode total (which contains all 3 calls + boot). The source shows the
194	hygiene rule from USER_GUIDE 4.2: anchor the kernel through memory inside
195	the marker span.
196	
197	- Key files: `demo/roi_rules/{main.c,Makefile,check.sh}`, top `Makefile`, `README.md`
198	- Pass: check.sh asserts `cycles(hybrid) < cycles(cycle) / 3`.
199	- Deps: none.
200	
201	## 8. diagnose
202	
203	State: TODO
204	Modes: hybrid (driver features, no new guest code needed - reuse the hello ELF).
205	
206	The debugging workflow as a script. check.sh exercises, in order:
207	`--dry-run` (asserts 2 resolved command lines), `--print-memmap` (asserts
208	the DRAM/V-scratch rows), `--log-level 1` (asserts the `[andesim] mmap`
209	line), `--log-file` (asserts timestamped, level-tagged lines land in the
210	file), and one forced leg failure that must leave a repro bundle
211	(`[andesim] repro: kept run artifacts at ...` -> assert `manifest.txt`
212	exists there). Open point for the build session: pick the most reliable
213	quick failure (candidate: a `--pc-end` that never retires, with a short
214	timeout).
215	
216	- Key files: `demo/diagnose/{Makefile,check.sh}`, top `Makefile`, `README.md`
217	- Pass: every assertion in check.sh.
218	- Deps: none. Reference: USER_GUIDE 5.5, 5.6, 5.10, 8.
219	
220	## 9. rv32
221	
222	State: TODO
223	Modes: fast only (no rv32 cycle engine installed; hybrid rejects rv32 by design).
224	
225	The rv32 runtime flavor and engine auto-select. Build hello against
226	`build/runtime/rv32` (`-march=rv32gc -mabi=ilp32d`), run `--mode fast` with
227	no `--engine`, and show the driver picked `qemu32` from the ELF width.
228	
229	- Key files: `demo/rv32/{main.c,Makefile}`, top `Makefile`, `README.md`
230	- Pass: hello output + exit code propagated; `--log-level 1` (or

255	State: BLOCKED (engine not installed)

271

276	## 12. atomic
277	
278	State: TODO
279	Modes: fast, cycle, hybrid (marker + pc).
280	Origin: vsim-demo-new `atomic-test`.
281	
282	LR/SC + AMO contract on every engine - nothing in the suite touches the A
283	extension today. Four tests in a `noinline` `atomic_kernel()` inside the
284	ROI: (T1) LR/SC pair succeeds and commits; (T2) after an SC consumes the
285	reservation, a second SC to the same address must fail and must not write;
286	(T3) `amoswap.w` returns old, writes new; (T4) 5x `amoadd.w` +7 on 100

288	with a same-hart store, which the ISA leaves implementation-defined (QEMU's
289	value-compare cmpxchg and the RTL monitor may legitimately diverge);

302	
303	State: TODO
304	Modes: fast + cycle only (expected-fail demo; hybrid's pass signal is a

306	Origin: vsim-demo-new `negative_test`.

308	A faulting guest must fail loudly on every engine. main prints a banner,
309	then executes an illegal instruction (`.insn r 0x7f, 0, 0, x0, x0, x0`,
310	fallback `unimp` if engines disagree on mcause). The runtime already does
311	the rest: `handler.c` prints `[ERROR] Trap occurred! ... mcause: 0x2` and
312	`_exit(mcause)`, so the driver exits 2. The `run:` target inverts (`!`) so
313	a correct fault reads as success; `check.sh` (memsize assert helper)
314	asserts rc==2 AND `Trap occurred` on stderr for both the fast and cycle
315	legs - loud failure if the guest does NOT trap or the cause differs.
316	
317	- Key files: `demo/trap/{main.c,Makefile,check.sh}`, top `Makefile`, `README.md`
318	- Pass: check.sh green on both legs, on every engine.

327	C++ on the andesim runtime, unblocked and demoed. Runtime side (andesim
328	commit `946e2e3`, TDD'd by `tests/vplat/test_vplat_cpp.sh`, 12/12 vplat
329	scripts green): crt0 keeps the direct `init_mtvec` call (that name
330	reference is what extracts handler.o from `libandesim_runtime.a`, and
331	the trap vector is live before any ctor) then walks `.init_array` via
332	newlib's `__libc_init_array`; `andesim.ld` PROVIDEs the array bounds

336	is untouched); main's return routes through `exit()` (C++
337	return-from-main == exit(rc): atexit + static dtors run). Demo side:
338	the static ctor assembles the "CPP" tag into a `std::string` before
339	main; the vsim ROI re-checks the tag from the RTL (the object's bytes
340	crossed the handoff), grows a `std::vector` on the newlib heap and
341	prints the runtime-composed `CPP_OK` inside the ROI; `CPP_DTOR_OK`

369	(`smu.hpp`), so the source demo's core-count read (SYSTEMCFG 0xf0100008)

372	- Key files: `demo/smp/{main.c,Makefile}`, top `Makefile`, `README.md`;

379	State: BLOCKED (vsim platform has no interrupt controllers)

381	Origin: vsim-demo-new `platform` (pit/plic/aia interrupt demos).

383	`vsim_andesim/src/platform/` models only UART, SMU and SimControl - no

# andesim-demo test roadmap

Each entry is one independent demo. One session builds ONE demo, then flips
its State and commits. States: `TODO`, `IN PROGRESS`, `DONE`, `BLOCKED`.

Conventions (same as the existing demos):

- Layout: `demo/<name>/main.c` + `demo/<name>/Makefile`; host-side checks go
  in `demo/<name>/check.sh` (the `memsize` precedent).
- Top-level `Makefile` gets `run-<name>` and the per-mode targets; `README.md`
  gets a short section describing what the demo proves.
- Pass signal: either the guest prints `<NAME>_OK` from inside the ROI, or
  `check.sh` asserts on the driver's output. Every demo must fail loudly.
- Demos run on every mode where the feature exists (some are hybrid-only or
  fast-only; each entry says which).

Priority = file order. 1-3 are headline USER_GUIDE features with zero demo
coverage today.

---

## 0. ok-grep: assert the *_OK line on every run target

State: TODO
Modes: all (harness change, no new guest code).

The 2026-07-16 fpga_l3 bring-up proved the "fail loudly" convention has a
hole: rvv, fp and syscall print their *_OK from inside the ROI, but their
`run` targets only propagate the exit code -- on hybrid the run ends at the
exit trigger, so a run whose in-ROI output silently VANISHED still exits 0.
That exact failure shipped: a coherence-manager RTL wedge dropped all in-ROI
UART output on ax46mpv_fpga_l3 and three demos kept "passing"; only
demo/cache had check.sh teeth (vsim_andesim 9be968a fixed the wedge).
Deliverable: each demo whose pass signal is a printed marker greps for it in
the run target (or gets a small check.sh), so lost output = red sweep.

- Key files: demo/{rvv,fp,syscall,lm,lm_slave,hvm_slave,cpp}/Makefile
  (or per-demo check.sh), README.md.
- Pass: `make check-all-engines` fails if any *_OK line goes missing.
- Deps: none.

---

## 1. hotloops

State: DONE
Modes: hybrid (pc trigger); the detector itself runs fast.

Measure a binary you cannot edit. `main.c` has one known hot loop (a
checksum over an array, >=10 iterations) and NO ROI markers. `check.sh`
runs `$(ANDESIM)/build/hotloops --min-iters 10 <elf>`, asserts the report
names the hot function, extracts the ready `measure:` line (a
`--pc-start`/`--pc-end` pair), and pastes it into
`./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger pc ...`. Closed loop: the detector's
output feeds the measurement command with no human guessing.

- Key files: `demo/hotloops/{main.c,Makefile,check.sh}`, top `Makefile`, `README.md`
- Pass: check.sh sees the hot function in the hotloops report AND a
  `[andesim] N cycles` line from the hybrid run using the reported PCs.
- Deps: none. Reference: USER_GUIDE 4.3, docs/hotloops.md.

## 2. verify

State: DONE
Modes: hybrid only (marker trigger).

Trust the figure. A state-heavy workload (GPR churn, scalar FP math under
RTZ, a strip-mined RVV loop, CSR writes staged before AND inside the ROI)
runs with `--verify`: andesim re-runs the ELF on pure QEMU up to the ROI
exit and compares the drained state field by field against the cycle
engine. Two builds from one source: `verify.elf` must PASS; the teeth are
`verify_taint.elf`, identical except one instruction sampling `mcycle`
into `t6` at the exit marker -- engine-divergent by design, so verify
must FAIL, name exactly `x31`, and exit non-zero. In the sweep the demo
is V-gated (`NEED_V`): the kernel uses RVV intrinsics.

- Key files: `demo/verify/{main.c,Makefile,check.sh}`, top `Makefile`, `README.md`
- Pass: check.sh asserts `[state-diff] PASS` + `[verify] PASS: vsim drain
  matches the QEMU oracle` on the clean build, and rc!=0 +
  `[state-diff] x31:` + `FAIL: 1 mismatch` on the taint build.
- Deps: none. Reference: USER_GUIDE 5.7.

## 3. kanata

State: TODO
Modes: hybrid only.

See the pipeline of exactly the ROI. A small kernel runs with
`--kanata roi.kanata --objdump kernel.S` (the dump generated at build time
with `objdump -d`). Users open the file in Konata; check.sh proves it is
well-formed without a GUI.

- Key files: `demo/kanata/{main.c,Makefile,check.sh}`, top `Makefile`, `README.md`
- Pass: check.sh asserts the Kanata header line, that a known kernel
  mnemonic from the objdump is embedded, and the trace is non-trivial
  (more than a handful of retired instructions).
- Constraint to demo: marker mode needs exactly ONE exit marker in the ELF
  (more -> andesim errors and points at `--trigger pc`).
- Deps: none. Reference: USER_GUIDE 5.8.

## 4. engines

State: DONE
Modes: the whole suite, once per installed vsim engine.

One suite, N cores - design-space switching, not a new demo dir. Every
demo's cycle/hybrid target already takes `ENGINE=<id>`, so the deliverable
is the sweep: `make check-all-engines` runs the aggregate `check` once per
vsim engine parsed from `andesim list engines` at run time (restrict with
`SWEEP_ENGINES="vsim:a ..."`) and prints a per-engine OK/FAILED summary.
Demos are capability-gated per engine from the driver's own output: the
lm*/hvm* demos skip when the engine's resolved hybrid plan (`--dry-run`)
carries no ILM/DLM/HVM sidecar args (`ax46mpv_advanced` has none), and rvv
skips when the engine's `list engines` row shows no VLEN.

- Key files: top `Makefile` (`check-all-engines`), `README.md`
- Pass: `make check-all-engines` exits 0. Teeth: a bogus engine in
  SWEEP_ENGINES makes the sweep report FAILED and exit nonzero.
- Deps: none.

## 5. fp

State: DONE
Modes: fast, cycle, hybrid (marker + pc).

Scalar FP state transport - fills the coverage gap next to `rvv` (which is
integer-V only). The QEMU phase sets a non-default rounding mode (`frm` =
RTZ) and raises a sticky `fflags` bit; the vsim ROI computes a
rounding-mode-sensitive result and checks: the result matches
expected-for-RTZ, and the pre-ROI sticky flag is still set. Proves
`fcsr` (+ `mstatus.FS`) crossed the handoff.

- Key files: `demo/fp/{main.c,Makefile}`, top `Makefile`, `README.md`
- Pass: guest prints `FP_OK`.
- Deps: none.

## 6. cache

State: DONE
Modes: hybrid (marker), two variants of one source.

Why timing-config transport matters. The same kernel is built twice from
one `main.c`: variant A keeps crt0's cache enable (transported
`mcache_ctl`), variant B writes `mcache_ctl = 0` before the ROI. check.sh
runs both hybrid measurements and asserts the uncached figure is much
larger. Doubles as a write-mask demo: the restore carries variant B's
disable only because the program itself wrote the CSR.

- Key files: `demo/cache/{main.c,Makefile,check.sh}`, top `Makefile`, `README.md`
- Pass: check.sh asserts `cycles(off) > 2 * cycles(on)` (calibrate the
  factor once real numbers exist).
- Deps: none. Reference: USER_GUIDE section 6 ("Config that matters for
  timing rides along").

### 6b. cache: L2C/L3C MMIO transport leg

State: DONE (2026-07-15)
Modes: hybrid only (marker) -- fast never leaves QEMU's stub, cycle never
leaves the RTL; only hybrid crosses the boundary under test.

Prove the platform shared-cache registers at 0xE0500000 ride the handoff:
the QEMU leg stages Control policy bits (RMW), HPM Control 0 and
WAYMASK0-4; the vsim ROI reads them back FROM THE RTL and prints
`L2C_OK`/`L3C_OK` before the exit marker. Separate tests per cache level
(one source, `-DSHC_L3`): the block is the L2C on 45-series engines, the
L3C on 46/66. Engine-gated by the `list engines` CACHE column (from
`--describe shared_cache_*`, which the vsim gate derives from the RTL's
`NDS_L2C/L3C_CACHE_SIZE_KB`). RO registers (Configuration, INITSTATUS)
and side-effect registers (CCTL command, W1C error) are excluded by
design. Passes on ax66_makatau (live 512K L3C); SKIPs naming the RTL
config on ax45mpv_premium/ax46mpv_advanced (built size 0). Companion
changes: vsim gate extension + Control policy-bit merge + describe keys;
driver descriptor/plan `l2c_base=`/verify mask/CACHE column.

- Key files: `demo/cache/{l2c.c,Makefile,check.sh}`, `README.md`;
  vsim_andesim `src/hybrid/{shared_cache_config.hpp,resume_driver.hpp}`,
  `src/{simulator.hpp,main.cpp}`; andesim
  `driver/{engine_descriptor.hpp,run_plan.cpp,state_diff.cpp,cmd_list.cpp}`;
  ABI `hybrid/state_abi.h` (`HYBRID_L2C_CTRL_POLICY_MASK`).
- Pass: `make check-cache ENGINE=vsim:ax66_makatau` prints
  `[PASS] hybrid L3C transport (L3:512K)`; ax45/ax46 print the
  RTL-config SKIP.
- Deps: none.

## 7. roi_rules

State: TODO
Modes: hybrid (marker + pc) vs cycle as the reference.

Trigger semantics and measurement hygiene, executable. A `noinline` kernel
is called 3 times; both triggers are one-shot, so the measured window is
the FIRST call only. check.sh asserts the hybrid figure is far below the
cycle-mode total (which contains all 3 calls + boot). The source shows the
hygiene rule from USER_GUIDE 4.2: anchor the kernel through memory inside
the marker span.

- Key files: `demo/roi_rules/{main.c,Makefile,check.sh}`, top `Makefile`, `README.md`
- Pass: check.sh asserts `cycles(hybrid) < cycles(cycle) / 3`.
- Deps: none.

## 8. diagnose

State: TODO
Modes: hybrid (driver features, no new guest code needed - reuse the hello ELF).

The debugging workflow as a script. check.sh exercises, in order:
`--dry-run` (asserts 2 resolved command lines), `--print-memmap` (asserts
the DRAM/V-scratch rows), `--log-level 1` (asserts the `[andesim] mmap`
line), `--log-file` (asserts timestamped, level-tagged lines land in the
file), and one forced leg failure that must leave a repro bundle
(`[andesim] repro: kept run artifacts at ...` -> assert `manifest.txt`
exists there). Open point for the build session: pick the most reliable
quick failure (candidate: a `--pc-end` that never retires, with a short
timeout).

- Key files: `demo/diagnose/{Makefile,check.sh}`, top `Makefile`, `README.md`
- Pass: every assertion in check.sh.
- Deps: none. Reference: USER_GUIDE 5.5, 5.6, 5.10, 8.

## 9. rv32

State: TODO
Modes: fast only (no rv32 cycle engine installed; hybrid rejects rv32 by design).

The rv32 runtime flavor and engine auto-select. Build hello against
`build/runtime/rv32` (`-march=rv32gc -mabi=ilp32d`), run `--mode fast` with
no `--engine`, and show the driver picked `qemu32` from the ELF width.

- Key files: `demo/rv32/{main.c,Makefile}`, top `Makefile`, `README.md`
- Pass: hello output + exit code propagated; `--log-level 1` (or
  `--dry-run`) shows qemu32 was selected.
- Deps: needs an rv32-capable compiler (separate riscv32 gcc or multilib);
  the Makefile must skip with a clear message if the toolchain cannot do
  rv32.

## 10. gdb

State: TODO
Modes: fast first; cycle as a stretch goal.

Attach a debugger, scripted. fast: launch `--gdb` in the background, drive
`gdb-multiarch` in batch mode (`-ex 'target remote :1234'`, break at a
symbol, continue, print a variable, kill). cycle: needs `$ICEMAN` pointing
at an OpenOCD 0.12+ wrapper speaking remote_bitbang (the Andes-bundled
0.10 has a known bug against this DTM) - build only if the host has it.

- Key files: `demo/gdb/{main.c,Makefile,check.sh}`, top `Makefile`, `README.md`
- Pass: the gdb batch log shows the breakpoint hit and the expected
  variable value. check.sh skips (with a message) when gdb/OpenOCD are
  missing.
- Deps: none in-repo; host tools required. Build last.

## 11. priv

State: BLOCKED (engine not installed)
Modes: hybrid.

S/U-mode handoff: drop privilege before the ROI, prove the level and the
PMP mirror crossed. Requires the S/U-capable `ax66_makatau` engine paired
with QEMU `-cpu andes-ax66`; `./andesim list engines` currently shows only
the two M-mode-only engines. Unblock by installing that engine, then spec
the demo.

- Key files: `demo/priv/{main.c,Makefile}`, top `Makefile`, `README.md`
- Pass: guest running in S-mode (or U-mode) inside the ROI prints `PRIV_OK`.
- Deps: ax66_makatau engine install.

---

the rest: `handler.c` prints `[ERROR] Trap occurred! ... mcause: 0x2` and
`_exit(mcause)`, so the driver exits 2. The `run:` target inverts (`!`) so
a correct fault reads as success; `check.sh` (memsize assert helper)
asserts rc==2 AND `Trap occurred` on stderr for both the fast and cycle
legs - loud failure if the guest does NOT trap or the cause differs.

- Key files: `demo/trap/{main.c,Makefile,check.sh}`, top `Makefile`, `README.md`
- Pass: check.sh green on both legs, on every engine.
- Deps: none.

## 14. cpp

State: DONE (2026-07-15)
Modes: fast, cycle, hybrid (marker + pc).
Origin: vsim-demo-new `cpp`.

C++ on the andesim runtime, unblocked and demoed. Runtime side (andesim
commit `946e2e3`, TDD'd by `tests/vplat/test_vplat_cpp.sh`, 12/12 vplat
scripts green): crt0 keeps the direct `init_mtvec` call (that name
reference is what extracts handler.o from `libandesim_runtime.a`, and
the trap vector is live before any ctor) then walks `.init_array` via
newlib's `__libc_init_array`; `andesim.ld` PROVIDEs the array bounds
ABOVE `_edata` -- crt0 zeroes `[_edata, _end)` before the walk, so
arrays after `.data` would be wiped; `andesim.specs` adds
crtbegin/crtend (the g++ driver injects `-lstdc++ -lm` itself, so *lib
is untouched); main's return routes through `exit()` (C++
return-from-main == exit(rc): atexit + static dtors run). Demo side:
the static ctor assembles the "CPP" tag into a `std::string` before
main; the vsim ROI re-checks the tag from the RTL (the object's bytes
crossed the handoff), grows a `std::vector` on the newlib heap and
prints the runtime-composed `CPP_OK` inside the ROI; `CPP_DTOR_OK`
prints after main returns (fast/cycle only -- hybrid ends at the exit
marker). The ROI kernel is `extern "C"`: the pc trigger resolves
symbols by name, so `cpp_roi`/`cpp_roi_end` must stay unmangled.
PASS on all four legs x all three engines (see README matrix).

- Key files: `demo/cpp/{main.cpp,Makefile}`, `Make.var` (adds CXX), top
  `Makefile`, `README.md`; andesim `runtime/{crt0.S,handler.c,andesim.ld,
  andesim.specs}` + `tests/fixtures/vplat_cpp.cpp` +
  `tests/vplat/test_vplat_cpp.sh` + USER_GUIDE 4.1 (other repo).
- Pass: guest prints `CPP_OK` composed by the static ctor inside the
  ROI on every mode; `CPP_DTOR_OK` + exit 0 on fast/cycle.
- Deps: none (runtime change landed).

## 15. smp

State: BLOCKED (no multi-hart engine registered)
Modes: cycle first; hybrid needs driver work.
Origin: vsim-demo-new `smp-test` (spinlock hello, per-hart caches,
shared-cache coherence).

Every registered engine is single-hart (`NDS_NHART=1`). Multi-hart RTL
configs exist (`ax45mpv_mp2`, `ax66_mp2`, NHART=2) but no engine is built
or registered from them. The runtime parks secondary harts
(`CRT0_MULTIPLE_HARTS=0`; they write 0x01234571 to SimControl and spin),
and the hybrid handoff transports one hart's state. Unblock path: build +
register an mp2 engine, rebuild the runtime with `CRT0_MULTIPLE_HARTS=1`,
then teach the handoff N harts. The vsim platform already models the SMU
(`smu.hpp`), so the source demo's core-count read (SYSTEMCFG 0xf0100008)
would work. Pairs naturally with the L2C/L3C work from entry 6b.

- Key files: `demo/smp/{main.c,Makefile}`, top `Makefile`, `README.md`;
  engine + runtime + driver work outside this repo.
- Pass: per-hart prints under a spinlock + a shared-cache coherence check.
- Deps: mp2 engine install; CRT0_MULTIPLE_HARTS runtime; driver handoff.

## 16. irq

State: BLOCKED (vsim platform has no interrupt controllers)
Modes: fast-only today, which is not worth a demo; needs cycle/hybrid.
Origin: vsim-demo-new `platform` (pit/plic/aia interrupt demos).

`vsim_andesim/src/platform/` models only UART, SMU and SimControl - no
PLIC, PLMT or PIT. QEMU's ae350 has andes_plic (0xe4000000) and andes_plmt
(0xe6000000), so an interrupt demo would run on fast but can never run a
cycle or hybrid leg. The source demos also lean on an `INT_TRIGGER`
sim-control backdoor (0xe0080020) that andesim's SimControl does not
provide. Unblock path: model the PLMT first (the machine timer is the
smallest useful interrupt source), then a timer-interrupt-inside-the-ROI
demo; PLIC/external sources later.

- Key files: `demo/irq/{main.c,Makefile}`, top `Makefile`, `README.md`;
  vsim_andesim platform model work outside this repo.
- Pass: ISR flag set by a timer interrupt taken inside the ROI; `IRQ_OK`.
- Deps: vsim_andesim PLMT (then PLIC) model.

## Port study: no port needed / not portable

Already covered, no port:

- `hello`, `coremark`, `dhrystone`, `rvv`, `syscall` - direct equivalents
  in SUBDIRS (ours add ROI markers, any-VLEN strip-mining, the uncached
  SimControl syscall window).
- `lm_test`, `hvm_test` - covered by `lm`/`lm_slave`/`lm_dma` and
  `hvm_slave`/`hvm_dma`. The old demos filled the memories through a
  sim-control "custom master" backdoor (0xe0080000 = 0xabcdeX); ours use
  the real transports (hart-local view, bus slave aperture, ATCDMAC300).
- `platform/uart_demo` - every demo's printf already exercises UART2.
- `hybrid`, `savable_feat` - the driver's hybrid mode plus the `verify`
  demo ARE the save/restore story; the driver has no user-facing
  `--save`/`--resume`, and adding one is a driver feature, not a demo.

Not portable:

- `ace`, `ace-rvv` - need the COPILOT toolflow (`.eca` for the assembler)
  plus a csim model (`libaceasim.a`) baked into the simulator build, and
  QEMU cannot execute ACE custom instructions, so fast mode, hybrid
  staging and the `--verify` oracle all break by construction. ax66 RTL
  has `NDS_ACE_SUPPORT=no` (ax45/ax46 have `yes`, but the generated
  instructions must match what COPILOT put into the RTL).
- `acervv46quad` - sources missing upstream (its Makefile references
  absent `.ace`/`.c` files and a private GEN_API tool).

# Shared configuration
-include Make.var

# Demos that run on every andesim mode (fast / cycle / hybrid).
SUBDIRS := demo/hello demo/lm demo/lm_slave demo/lm_dma \
           demo/hvm_slave demo/hvm_dma demo/rvv demo/fp demo/cache \
           demo/verify demo/syscall demo/coremark demo/dhrystone demo/memsize \
           demo/cpp

RUN_TARGETS := $(patsubst demo/%,run-%,$(SUBDIRS))

# RUN_TARGETS are deliberately NOT .PHONY: make never matches pattern
# rules (run-%) against .PHONY targets.
.PHONY: all run check check-all-engines clean $(SUBDIRS)

all: $(SUBDIRS)

$(SUBDIRS):
	$(MAKE) -C $@

run: $(RUN_TARGETS)

run-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/$* run

# Forward per-mode targets, e.g. `make hello-fast` -> demo/hello hello-fast.
hello-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/hello $@

lm-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/lm $@

lm_slave-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/lm_slave $@

lm_dma-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/lm_dma $@

hvm_slave-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/hvm_slave $@

hvm_dma-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/hvm_dma $@

rvv-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/rvv $@

fp-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/fp $@

cache-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/cache $@

verify-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/verify $@

syscall-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/syscall $@

coremark-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/coremark $@

dhrystone-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/dhrystone $@

memsize-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/memsize $@

cpp-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/cpp $@

# Aggregate check: every demo that defines its own `check` runs it (real
# asserts); the rest are asserted to `run` cleanly (exit 0) across all modes.
# Continues past failures and reports a summary. Heavy -- coremark/dhrystone
# run their full cycle/hybrid legs. For one demo use `make check-<name>`.
check:
	@fail=""; \
	for dir in $(SUBDIRS); do \
	  echo "########## $$dir ##########"; \
	  if $(MAKE) -C $$dir -n check >/dev/null 2>&1; then \
	    $(MAKE) -C $$dir check || fail="$$fail $$dir"; \
	  elif $(MAKE) -C $$dir run; then \
	    echo "[PASS] $$dir: run exits 0 (no asserts)"; \
	  else \
	    echo "[FAIL] $$dir: run failed"; fail="$$fail $$dir"; \
	  fi; \
	done; \
	echo "===================================="; \
	if [ -z "$$fail" ]; then echo "ALL DEMOS OK"; \
	else echo "FAILED DEMOS:$$fail"; exit 1; fi

# ---- Engine sweep --------------------------------------------------------
# Demos that need hardware not every engine has. The sweep skips them on an
# engine whose resolved hybrid plan (--dry-run) carries no ILM/DLM/HVM
# sidecar args, or whose `list engines` row shows no VLEN.
NEED_LM  := demo/lm demo/lm_slave demo/lm_dma
NEED_HVM := demo/hvm_slave demo/hvm_dma
NEED_V   := demo/rvv demo/verify

# Run the aggregate `check` once per installed vsim engine -- the engine set
# is parsed from `andesim list engines` at run time (rv64 rows; the demos
# are rv64 builds). Restrict it with SWEEP_ENGINES="vsim:a vsim:b". Fails if
# any engine fails any demo it is capable of.
check-all-engines:
	@engines="$(SWEEP_ENGINES)"; \
	if [ -z "$$engines" ]; then \
	  engines=$$("$(ANDESIM_BIN)" list engines 2>/dev/null \
	             | awk '$$2 == "vsim" && $$4 == 64 { print $$1 }'); \
	fi; \
	if [ -z "$$engines" ]; then \
	  echo "no rv64 vsim engine installed (see: andesim list engines)"; exit 1; \
	fi; \
	$(MAKE) -C demo/hello hello.elf >/dev/null; \
	summary=""; bad=""; \
	for eng in $$engines; do \
	  plan=$$("$(ANDESIM_BIN)" run --mode hybrid --trigger marker \
	          --engine "$$eng" --dry-run demo/hello/hello.elf </dev/null 2>&1); \
	  vlen=$$("$(ANDESIM_BIN)" list engines 2>/dev/null \
	          | awk -v e="$$eng" '$$1 == e { print $$5 }'); \
	  skips=""; \
	  echo "$$plan" | grep -q "ilm_size=[1-9]" || skips="$$skips $(NEED_LM)"; \
	  echo "$$plan" | grep -q "hvm_size=[1-9]" || skips="$$skips $(NEED_HVM)"; \
	  case "$$vlen" in ""|-|0) skips="$$skips $(NEED_V)";; esac; \
	  dirs=""; \
	  for d in $(SUBDIRS); do \
	    case " $$skips " in *" $$d "*) ;; *) dirs="$$dirs $$d";; esac; \
	  done; \
	  echo "#################### ENGINE $$eng ####################"; \
	  if [ -n "$$skips" ]; then echo "[SKIP] $$eng lacks the hardware for:$$skips"; fi; \
	  if $(MAKE) check ENGINE="$$eng" SUBDIRS="$$dirs"; then \
	    summary="$$summary\n  $$eng: OK (skipped:$${skips:- none})"; \
	  else \
	    summary="$$summary\n  $$eng: FAILED"; bad="$$bad $$eng"; \
	  fi; \
	done; \
	echo "#################### ENGINE SWEEP ####################"; \
	printf "engines:$$summary\n"; \
	if [ -n "$$bad" ]; then echo "FAILED ENGINES:$$bad"; exit 1; fi

# Single demo: its own `check` if defined, else assert `run` exits 0.
check-%:
	@if $(MAKE) -C demo/$* -n check >/dev/null 2>&1; then \
	  $(MAKE) -C demo/$* check; \
	else \
	  echo "demo/$*: no asserts -- running to assert exit 0"; \
	  $(MAKE) -C demo/$* run; \
	fi

clean:
	@for dir in $(SUBDIRS); do $(MAKE) -C $$dir clean; done

Author: Nick Hung <nick@andestech.com>
Date:   Thu Jul 16 05:04:11 2026 +0800

    feat(runtime): vlinux Linux-runtime proxy kernel + llama.cpp hybrid ROI (behavioral)
    
    Adds runtime/linux/ (vlinux): a small M-mode proxy kernel (ELF loader,
    Linux initial-stack/auxv builder, ~30-syscall dispatch table over the
    existing HTIF window) that lets a prebuilt static-glibc RISC-V binary
    run unmodified on andesim fast/cycle/hybrid, driven by a new `andesim
    run --runtime linux` driver flag (driver/manifest.{hpp,cpp},
    driver/tempdir.{hpp,cpp}).
    
    Primary target, verified end to end: llama.cpp's `llama-completion`
    generating real text from Bonsai-4B-Q1_0.gguf on the fast leg, and
    hybrid mode measuring real cycle counts for one transformer matmul
    (driver/elf_syms.{hpp,cpp}'s find_roi_markers + vsim's existing
    --hybrid-exit-pc flag work around vsim's static-ELF marker pre-scan
    not seeing a dynamically-loaded app; new --step-timeout-ms flag raises
    the hardcoded 90s per-leg timeout for a real matmul's cycle count).
    
    Getting a real llama.cpp build through hybrid's engine-synced,
    ELEN=32-enforcing QEMU leg needed four small upstream ggml fixes
    (not part of this repo; documented in docs/llama_roi_howto.md and
    applied directly to the /home/nick/work/llama.cpp checkout) for code
    that assumed the RVV spec's ELEN>=64 floor or a full LMUL=8 vector
    FPU datapath, neither of which this target implements.
    
    Full history, verified facts, and each feature's test contract are in
    ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md (U0 through U9, all DONE) -- this single
    commit lands that whole already-tested effort at once since none of
    it had been committed incrementally. One known, documented gap
    carried over unfixed: glibc's exit() crashes in its own
    __run_exit_handlers walk on this target (a vendor-toolchain question,
    not a vlinux bug -- see ROADMAP U4), tolerated by every affected test.
    
    Structural refactors folded in: runtime/htif_client.{c,h} (extracted
    from vplat_syscalls.c so vplat and vlinux share one HTIF window
    client) and driver/strutil.hpp's parse_positive_int (extracted from
    driver/cmd_profile.cpp so --limit/--min-iters/--step-timeout-ms share
    one CLI-knob parser instead of three copies).

content.content:
1	# Measuring one llama.cpp kernel iteration under andesim hybrid mode
2	
3	This is the companion doc USER_GUIDE.md section 11 points to: the exact
4	patch that puts ROI markers around a matmul (or a short run of
5	consecutive matmuls) inside llama.cpp, how the target was chosen, and
6	the upstream `ggml` fixes a real build needs before it survives the
7	cycle-accurate leg's ELEN=32 vector unit.
8	
9	Confirmed end to end:
10	- 2026-07-16: single iteration (K=51, layer 7's V projection), on
11	  `vsim:ax45mpv_premium` (ELEN=32) -- **6528953 cycles**, stable across
12	  two independent hybrid runs.
13	- 2026-07-16: two consecutive iterations (K=51..52, V then K
14	  projection), same engine -- **13040043 cycles** (~2x the
15	  single-iteration figure, as expected for two similarly-sized matmuls
16	  back to back). See section 6 for how to pick N.
17	- 2026-07-16: single iteration (K=51), on `vsim:ax46mpv_fpga_l3`
18	  (ELEN=64, VLEN=1024, first engine with a real L3 cache) -- **4476168
19	  cycles**, with the PRISTINE upstream `ggml` source (none of section
20	  4's three ggml patches applied -- this engine's real ELEN=64 vector
21	  unit runs the original e64 code natively). Fewer cycles than
22	  ax45mpv_premium's for the SAME node: the doubled VLEN does more work
23	  per vector instruction. See section 8 for this engine's build recipe
24	  and two DIFFERENT bugs that needed fixing to get there.
25	
26	## 1. Why the marker goes in ggml's dispatch loop, not llama.cpp's model code
27	
28	`ggml` builds its WHOLE computation graph first (`ggml_mul_mat()` just
29	appends a node), then executes it in one shot via a generic per-node
30	dispatch loop (`ggml_graph_compute_thread` -> `ggml_compute_forward`, in
31	`ggml/src/ggml-cpu/ggml-cpu.c`). Individual ops are not distinguishable
32	at the call site (e.g. the per-layer forward-pass code in
33	`src/models/qwen3.cpp` or similar) -- by the time any one op actually
34	*runs*, you are inside this generic loop, looking at a `ggml_tensor*`
35	with no easy way to tell "this is layer 7's V projection" apart from any
36	other `GGML_OP_MUL_MAT` node without counting.
37	
38	So the marker patch counts nodes and fires on the K-th one:
39	
40	```c
41	// ggml/src/ggml-cpu/ggml-cpu.c, inside ggml_compute_forward's switch:
42	case GGML_OP_MUL_MAT:
43	    {
44	#if defined(__riscv) && defined(ANDESIM_ROI_MUL_MAT_K)
45	        static int andesim_mul_mat_n = 0;
46	        const bool andesim_roi = (++andesim_mul_mat_n == ANDESIM_ROI_MUL_MAT_K);
47	        if (andesim_roi) andesim_ROI_begin();
48	#endif
49	        ggml_compute_forward_mul_mat(params, tensor);
50	#if defined(__riscv) && defined(ANDESIM_ROI_MUL_MAT_K)
51	        if (andesim_roi) andesim_ROI_end();
52	#endif
53	    } break;
54	```
55	
56	Also add near the top of the file:
57	
58	```c
59	#if defined(__riscv) && defined(ANDESIM_ROI_MUL_MAT_K)
60	#include <andesim/ROI.h>
61	#endif
62	```
63	
64	`ANDESIM_ROI_MUL_MAT_K` is a build-time `-D`, not a source edit -- picking
65	a different node to measure is a reconfigure, not a patch change (see
66	section 3). Both markers are HINT NOPs (`andesim_ROI_begin()`/`_end()`),
67	so this same binary still runs correctly, unmeasured, on any engine or on
68	silicon when the counter never reaches K (or when `ANDESIM_ROI_MUL_MAT_K`
69	is undefined -- the whole block compiles out).
70	
71	## 2. Counting the nodes
72	
73	Bonsai-4B (qwen3 architecture, 36 layers, 2560 embd) does 253 `MUL_MAT`
74	calls per token: 36 layers x 7 matmuls (Q, V, K, O-projection, FFN gate,
75	up, down -- confirmed via gdb breakpoint counting on a native x86 debug
76	build, not assumed from the layer count alone) + 1 final `lm_head`.
77	
78	## 3. Picking K: smallest matmul, not the first one that compiles
79	
80	The obvious first pick is any early node -- K=50 lands on layer 7's Q
81	projection (2560 -> 4096). It runs correctly (once the fixes in section 4
82	are applied) but is too large a computation for the cycle-accurate leg to
83	finish even inside a 900000ms (15 minute) `--step-timeout-ms` budget.
84	
85	Rather than guess a smaller K blindly, dump every node's operand shapes
86	for one real forward pass on a **native x86 build** (fast, no simulator
87	needed) with a throwaway diagnostic:
88	
89	```c
90	// temporary -- not committed; add right before ggml_compute_forward_mul_mat(...):
91	#if defined(ANDESIM_DUMP_MUL_MAT_SIZES)
92	{
93	    const struct ggml_tensor* s0 = tensor->src[0];
94	    const struct ggml_tensor* s1 = tensor->src[1];
95	    fprintf(stderr, "ANDESIM_MUL_MAT name=%s src0=%s[%lldx%lld] src1=[%lldx%lld]\n",
96	            tensor->name, ggml_type_name(s0->type),
97	            (long long) s0->ne[0], (long long) s0->ne[1],
98	            (long long) s1->ne[0], (long long) s1->ne[1]);
99	}
100	#endif
101	```
102	
103	```sh
104	cmake -B build-host -DCMAKE_C_FLAGS="-DANDESIM_DUMP_MUL_MAT_SIZES"
105	cmake --build build-host -j --target llama-completion
106	./build-host/bin/llama-completion -m models/Bonsai-4B-Q1_0.gguf -no-cnv \
107	  --prompt "The capital of France is" -n 1 -c 512 -t 1 2>&1 | grep ANDESIM_MUL_MAT
108	```
109	
110	Result, per layer: Q/O-projection and the FFN gate/up/down matmuls are
111	all 2560x4096..2560x9728 (the FFN matmuls are actually ~2.4x LARGER than
112	Q, not smaller -- do not assume "later in the layer means smaller"). The
113	K/V-projection (2560x1024, this model's grouped-query attention uses
114	fewer KV heads than Q heads) is the smallest matmul shape anywhere in the
115	architecture, ~4x fewer MACs than Q, ~9.6x fewer than the FFN matmuls,
116	and there is nothing smaller available in a standard transformer layer
117	(the `lm_head` is larger still: `2560 x vocab_size`).
118	
119	**Verified working value: `ANDESIM_ROI_MUL_MAT_K=51`** -- layer 7's V
120	projection, the very next node after the original K=50 pick. Completes
121	comfortably inside a 900000ms budget.
122	
123	If you retarget K, verify the object file actually recompiled with the
124	new value before spending 10+ minutes on a run that might still be
125	running the old K:
126	
127	```sh
128	python3 -c "
129	import json
130	for e in json.load(open('build-rv64-static/compile_commands.json')):
131	    if e['file'].endswith('ggml-cpu.c'):
132	        print(e['command']); break
133	" | grep -o 'ANDESIM_ROI_MUL_MAT_K=[0-9]*'
134	```
135	
136	(A stale-ccache-or-incomplete-incremental-rebuild gotcha cost real time
137	during this investigation: `compile_commands.json` showing the right flag
138	is necessary but was, once, not sufficient -- the `.o` had not actually
139	been regenerated. If a rebuild's *behavior* doesn't match what the
140	*compile command* implies, `rm -f` the exact `.o` path under
141	`build-rv64-static/ggml/src/CMakeFiles/ggml-cpu.dir/` and rebuild again
142	before doubting the fix itself.)
143	
144	## 4. Four fixes a real build needs before the cycle-accurate leg accepts it
145	
146	**These four fixes are specific to ELEN=32 engines** (`ax45mpv_premium`,
147	`ax46mpv_advanced`) and route around a vector-width limit those engines
148	genuinely have. On an ELEN=64 engine (`ax46mpv_fpga_l3`) none of this is
149	needed -- the pristine upstream `ggml` source already works, because the
150	assumption these patches route around (e64 support) is actually true
151	there. Do not apply section 4's patches when building for an ELEN=64
152	engine; see section 8 for what THAT engine needs instead.
153	
154	Hybrid's QEMU leg is engine-synced (`elen=32`, from the accurate
155	`-readconfig`) -- unlike fast mode's own hardcoded, unconstrained `-cpu
156	andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512` string, it actually enforces the real engine's
157	32-bit vector-element limit. A stock `GGML_RVV` build of `ggml` was
158	written assuming `v` implies the RVV-spec-mandated ELEN>=64 minimum, so
159	several code paths emit illegal 64-bit-element vector instructions this
160	target cannot execute. All four were found the same way: run the real
161	binary, catch the illegal-instruction trap (mcause=2), disassemble at the
162	exact `mepc`, fix, repeat.
163	
164	1. **`ggml_vec_dot_f16`/`ggml_vec_dot_bf16`** (`ggml/src/ggml-cpu/vec.cpp`):
165	   GCC auto-vectorizes their `double`-accumulated scalar fallback loop
166	   (taken because this build has neither `__riscv_zvfh` nor
167	   `__riscv_zvfbfwma`) into an illegal widening e64 reduce. Fix: add
168	   `__attribute__((target("arch=rv64gc")))` to just these two function
169	   definitions -- confirmed empirically that GCC's RISC-V port honors a
170	   function-level `target` attribute for suppressing this (the `optimize`
171	   attribute and `#pragma GCC push_options`/`optimize` do NOT work here --
172	   tried both, objdump showed no change either time).
173	
174	2. **`ggml_vec_cvar_f32`/`ggml_vec_soft_max_f32`** (same file): use an
175	   explicit `vfloat64m1_t` accumulator (`vfwredusum_vs_f32m2_f64m1`,
176	   widening reduce). Every other architecture's branch in these same two
177	   functions reduces in native f32 precision with a plain SIMD op, then
178	   widens ONE scalar partial-sum per chunk to `double` in ordinary C --
179	   the RISC-V branch was the only outlier, not a hardware requirement.
180	   Fix: rewrite to match the sibling pattern (`vfredusum_vs_f32m2_f32m1`,
181	   non-widening, then `sum += (ggml_float) partial` in scalar C). Zero e64,
182	   same numerics every other build already computes.
183	
184	3. **`quantize_row_q8_0`/`quantize_row_q8_1`**
185	   (`ggml/src/ggml-cpu/arch/riscv/quants.c`): hardcode `vfloat32m8_t`
186	   (LMUL=8) for `vfabs`/`vfredmax`, unconditionally, unlike every other
187	   quant kernel in the same file (which dispatch across
188	   vl1024/vl512/vl256/vl128 variants). `ax45mpv_premium`'s vector FPU
189	   datapath does not extend to LMUL=8 for floating-point ops specifically
190	   (a plain integer `vle32.v` load at the same LMUL=8 executes fine
191	   immediately before the float op faults -- this is FP-datapath-specific,
192	   not a blanket LMUL cap; correlates with the engine's `isa-vl4` config
193	   bit, though only vsim's RTL enforces it -- QEMU does not, which is why
194	   this one surfaces on vsim rather than QEMU1, unlike fixes 1/2/4). Fix:
195	   both functions now call their existing portable `_ref` scalar
196	   implementations (`ggml/src/ggml-quants.c`, already used as the non-RVV
197	   fallback everywhere) unconditionally -- this is activation
198	   quantization, called once per token row before the (still fully
199	   vectorized) dot-product loop reuses it, a trivial fraction of total
200	   matmul cost.
201	
202	4. **Diagnostic-path gap, not a ggml bug**: `runtime/handler.c`'s trap
203	   handler (shared by every andesim runtime, vplat and vlinux alike)
204	   calls `fprintf` then `_exit()`; `_exit()` never flushes stdio, so on a
205	   fully-buffered stderr (the vlinux syscall-backed stdio path) the whole
206	   diagnostic was silently lost on every trap. Fixed with an
207	   `fflush(stderr)` before `_exit()`, plus a raw `htif_uart_putc()`-based
208	   emergency print of `mcause`/`mepc`/`mtval` before even attempting
209	   `fprintf` (cheap insurance against a corrupted-state trap taking out
210	   `fprintf` itself). This is what made fix 3 possible to diagnose in the
211	   first place -- see `ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md`'s U9 section for the full
212	   trail.
213	
214	## 5. Reproducing the confirmed run
215	
216	```sh
217	# in llama.cpp:
218	cmake -B build-rv64-static \
219	  -DBUILD_SHARED_LIBS=OFF -DGGML_NATIVE=OFF -DGGML_OPENMP=OFF \
220	  -DGGML_RV_ZFH=OFF -DGGML_RV_ZVFH=OFF -DGGML_CPU_REPACK=OFF \
221	  -DCMAKE_C_FLAGS="-mext-zvlsseg -DANDESIM_ROI_MUL_MAT_K=51 -I /path/to/andesim/build/runtime/include" \
222	  -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS="-mext-zvlsseg -DANDESIM_ROI_MUL_MAT_K=51 -I /path/to/andesim/build/runtime/include"
223	cmake --build build-rv64-static -j --target llama-completion
224	
225	# in andesim:
226	./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --runtime linux --mem-size 2000M \
227	  --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium --step-timeout-ms 900000 \
228	  /path/to/llama.cpp/build-rv64-static/bin/llama-completion \
229	  -- -m /path/to/models/Bonsai-4B-Q1_0.gguf -no-cnv \
230	     --prompt "The capital of France is" -n 32 -c 512 -t 1
231	```
232	
233	Expected: `[andesim] 6528953 cycles`, identical across repeat runs.
234	
235	## 6. Measuring N consecutive iterations
236	
237	For a few consecutive matmuls instead of just one, set `ANDESIM_ROI_MUL_MAT_N`
238	alongside `ANDESIM_ROI_MUL_MAT_K` (both are build-time `-D`s -- no source
239	change). The marker begins at node K and ends at node K+N-1, so N=1
240	(the default when unset) is exactly the original single-iteration
241	behavior:
242	
243	```sh
244	cmake -B build-rv64-static ... \
245	  -DCMAKE_C_FLAGS="... -DANDESIM_ROI_MUL_MAT_K=51 -DANDESIM_ROI_MUL_MAT_N=2 ..." \
246	  -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS="... -DANDESIM_ROI_MUL_MAT_K=51 -DANDESIM_ROI_MUL_MAT_N=2 ..."
247	cmake --build build-rv64-static -j --target llama-completion
248	```
249	
250	Confirmed K=51..52 (V then K projection, both small): **13040043
251	cycles**, ~2x the single-iteration figure as expected.
252	
253	**Keep N small.** The cycle-accurate leg runs at ~9 kHz; N=1 on the V
254	projection alone already needs ~13 minutes of wall clock (hence
255	`--step-timeout-ms 900000`+). Including one of the large matmuls (Q, O,
256	or any FFN projection -- see section 3's size ranking) in the range
257	multiplies the cost accordingly; a whole token (253 matmuls) is not
258	practical this way. Pick a short, deliberately small run of the
259	smallest-available matmuls, exactly like section 3 already argues for
260	a single iteration.
261	
262	## 7. Dumping pipeline information (`--kanata`)
263	
264	`andesim run --mode hybrid --kanata <file>` (see USER_GUIDE.md section
265	5.8) writes a Kanata-format pipeline trace of the ROI, viewable in
266	[Konata](https://github.com/shioyadan/Konata):
267	
268	```sh
269	./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --runtime linux --mem-size 2000M \
270	  --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium --step-timeout-ms 900000 \
271	  --kanata /tmp/roi.kanata \
272	  /path/to/llama.cpp/build-rv64-static/bin/llama-completion \
273	  -- -m /path/to/models/Bonsai-4B-Q1_0.gguf -no-cnv \
274	     --prompt "The capital of France is" -n 32 -c 512 -t 1
275	```
276	
277	No source or build change needed beyond what section 5 already has --
278	`--kanata` reads the same ROI markers the cycle measurement uses.
279	Confirmed on the K=51 single-iteration build: a 651 MB, well-formed
280	Kanata trace (`Kanata 0004` header, ~43.8M lines, event counts
281	consistent with 6528953 cycles). The trace is large in proportion to
282	the cycle count -- expect a correspondingly bigger file for a
283	multi-iteration (N>1) ROI.
284	
285	**A real bug this surfaced, fixed as part of this work**: the driver's
286	`vsim_extra_args()` (`driver/hybrid.cpp`) unconditionally appended a
287	`--kanata-roi` flag alongside `--kanata` -- a flag that does not exist
288	anywhere in vsim (confirmed against vsim's own `--help` and its full
289	source tree), so every hybrid `--kanata` run failed immediately with
290	`Unrecognized option: --kanata-roi` before this fix. Root cause: vsim's
291	hybrid leg only ever executes the ROI in the first place (it resumes
292	at the trigger boundary and exits on the matching trigger), so plain
293	`--kanata` already produces exactly the "measured window only" trace
294	USER_GUIDE.md section 5.8 describes -- no separate "roi" flag was ever
295	needed on vsim's side. This had no automated-test coverage (the only
296	place `--kanata-roi` appeared besides the driver's own code was a
297	manually-gated block in `tests/e2e.sh` behind an unset-by-default
298	`KANATA_FILE` env var), so the bug was latent until `--kanata` was
299	actually exercised against a real vsim binary for the first time here.
300	
301	## 8. Building for an ELEN=64 engine (`ax46mpv_fpga_l3`)
302	
303	This engine's real ISA has Zca+Zcmp+Zcmt but NOT Zcd (compressed
304	double-precision FP load/store) -- confirmed via
305	`sim_ax46mpv_fpga_l3 --print-qemu-config`, the ground-truth source for
306	any engine's real capability set (never assume it from a same-family
307	engine's config; `ax46mpv_advanced`, sharing the same `cpp_wrapper`, is
308	single-bank-HVM and Zcd-agnostic in a way `ax46mpv_fpga_l3` is not).
309	GCC's default `rv64gc...` march sets the legacy monolithic `C` bit,
310	which implies Zcd -- so ordinary function prologues spilling
311	callee-saved FP registers (nothing ROI/vector-specific; this hit
312	`ggml_cpu_init`, generic ggml startup code) emitted `c.fsdsp`, illegal
313	on this chip. Two new CMake cache variables in
314	`ggml/src/ggml-cpu/CMakeLists.txt` let the march string target this
315	correctly, with the default (`GGML_RV_MARCH_LETTERS` unset ==
316	`"gc"`, `GGML_RV_ZC_EXTRA` unset == none) reproducing the EXACT prior
317	march string for every other engine, unchanged:
318	
319	```sh
320	# in llama.cpp (no vec.cpp/quants.c/march-restriction patches applied --
321	# pristine upstream source, section 4 is NOT needed on this engine):
322	cmake -B build-rv64-static \
323	  -DBUILD_SHARED_LIBS=OFF -DGGML_NATIVE=OFF -DGGML_OPENMP=OFF \
324	  -DGGML_RV_ZFH=OFF -DGGML_RV_ZVFH=OFF -DGGML_CPU_REPACK=OFF \
325	  -DGGML_RV_MARCH_LETTERS=g -DGGML_RV_ZC_EXTRA=zca_zcb_zcmp_zcmt \
326	  -DCMAKE_C_FLAGS="-mext-zvlsseg -DANDESIM_ROI_MUL_MAT_K=51 -I /path/to/andesim/build/runtime/include" \
327	  -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS="-mext-zvlsseg -DANDESIM_ROI_MUL_MAT_K=51 -I /path/to/andesim/build/runtime/include"
328	cmake --build build-rv64-static -j --target llama-completion
329	
330	# in andesim: this engine's cycle-accurate leg is MUCH slower in
331	# wall-clock terms than ax45mpv_premium's for the same node (several
332	# hundred x realtime vs ax45's tens of x) -- budget --step-timeout-ms
333	# generously; 900000 (the ax45mpv_premium-sized default) is NOT enough
334	# even for a single K=51 iteration on this engine.
335	./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --runtime linux --mem-size 2000M \
336	  --engine vsim:ax46mpv_fpga_l3 --step-timeout-ms 14400000 \
337	  /path/to/llama.cpp/build-rv64-static/bin/llama-completion \
338	  -- -m /path/to/models/Bonsai-4B-Q1_0.gguf -no-cnv \
339	     --prompt "The capital of France is" -n 32 -c 512 -t 1
340	```
341	
342	Expected: `[andesim] 4476168 cycles`.
343	
344	**A second, unrelated bug found getting here, fixed in the external
345	`vsim_andesim` repo, not andesim or llama.cpp**: this is the first
346	ax46mpv-family engine config with `NDS_HVM_BANKS=2` (every prior
347	ax46mpv config, e.g. `ax46mpv_advanced`, is single-bank).
348	`ax46mpv_cpu_cluster_subsystem.hpp`'s `set_hvm`/`get_hvm` only ever
349	wrote/read HVM bank0's hierarchical Verilated array, using the TOTAL
350	`_NDS_HVM_SIZE_KB` (both banks combined) as the length -- overflowing
351	bank0's actual (half-sized) array by the other half, corrupting heap
352	state that only surfaced later as an unrelated-looking SIGSEGV inside
353	`sc_core::sc_port_registry::construction_done()` during the NEXT
354	`sc_start()` elaboration call. Fixed by porting
355	`ax45mpv_premium_cpu_cluster_subsystem.hpp`'s already-correct 2-bank
356	split (same shared `hvm_bank_write`/`hvm_bank_read` helpers,
357	`lm_backdoor.hpp`, called twice with different `base` offsets) into
358	ax46mpv's wrapper, gated so the existing single-bank engine's behavior
359	is untouched. Rebuilt via `vsim_andesim/build_vsim.sh` (the repo's own
360	Docker/podman build, no manual host-side ninja invocation -- the
361	generated build files reference container-internal `/work/...` paths).
362	If a future engine changes any other previously-constant parameter
363	(cache presence/level, privilege levels, bank counts elsewhere), expect
364	a similar class of latent bug in whichever cpu_wrapper code path was
365	never exercised with that parameter varying.
