# Measuring one llama.cpp kernel iteration under andesim hybrid mode

This is the companion doc USER_GUIDE.md section 11 points to: the exact
patch that puts ROI markers around a matmul (or a short run of
consecutive matmuls) inside llama.cpp, how the target was chosen, and
the upstream `ggml` fixes a real build needs before it survives the
cycle-accurate leg's ELEN=32 vector unit.

Confirmed end to end:
- 2026-07-16: single iteration (K=51, layer 7's V projection), on
  `vsim:ax45mpv_premium` (ELEN=32) -- **6528953 cycles**, stable across
  two independent hybrid runs.
- 2026-07-16: two consecutive iterations (K=51..52, V then K
  projection), same engine -- **13040043 cycles** (~2x the
  single-iteration figure, as expected for two similarly-sized matmuls
  back to back). See section 6 for how to pick N.
- 2026-07-16: single iteration (K=51), on `vsim:ax46mpv_fpga_l3`
  (ELEN=64, VLEN=1024, first engine with a real L3 cache) -- **4476168
  cycles**, with the PRISTINE upstream `ggml` source (none of section
  4's three ggml patches applied -- this engine's real ELEN=64 vector
  unit runs the original e64 code natively). Fewer cycles than
  ax45mpv_premium's for the SAME node: the doubled VLEN does more work
  per vector instruction. See section 8 for this engine's build recipe
  and two DIFFERENT bugs that needed fixing to get there.

## 1. Why the marker goes in ggml's dispatch loop, not llama.cpp's model code

`ggml` builds its WHOLE computation graph first (`ggml_mul_mat()` just
appends a node), then executes it in one shot via a generic per-node
dispatch loop (`ggml_graph_compute_thread` -> `ggml_compute_forward`, in
`ggml/src/ggml-cpu/ggml-cpu.c`). Individual ops are not distinguishable
at the call site (e.g. the per-layer forward-pass code in
`src/models/qwen3.cpp` or similar) -- by the time any one op actually
*runs*, you are inside this generic loop, looking at a `ggml_tensor*`
with no easy way to tell "this is layer 7's V projection" apart from any
other `GGML_OP_MUL_MAT` node without counting.

So the marker patch counts nodes and fires on the K-th one:

```c
// ggml/src/ggml-cpu/ggml-cpu.c, inside ggml_compute_forward's switch:
case GGML_OP_MUL_MAT:
    {
#if defined(__riscv) && defined(ANDESIM_ROI_MUL_MAT_K)
        static int andesim_mul_mat_n = 0;
        const bool andesim_roi = (++andesim_mul_mat_n == ANDESIM_ROI_MUL_MAT_K);
        if (andesim_roi) andesim_ROI_begin();
#endif
        ggml_compute_forward_mul_mat(params, tensor);
#if defined(__riscv) && defined(ANDESIM_ROI_MUL_MAT_K)
        if (andesim_roi) andesim_ROI_end();
#endif
    } break;
```

Also add near the top of the file:

```c
#if defined(__riscv) && defined(ANDESIM_ROI_MUL_MAT_K)
#include <andesim/ROI.h>
#endif
```

`ANDESIM_ROI_MUL_MAT_K` is a build-time `-D`, not a source edit -- picking
a different node to measure is a reconfigure, not a patch change (see
section 3). Both markers are HINT NOPs (`andesim_ROI_begin()`/`_end()`),
so this same binary still runs correctly, unmeasured, on any engine or on
silicon when the counter never reaches K (or when `ANDESIM_ROI_MUL_MAT_K`
is undefined -- the whole block compiles out).

## 2. Counting the nodes

Bonsai-4B (qwen3 architecture, 36 layers, 2560 embd) does 253 `MUL_MAT`
calls per token: 36 layers x 7 matmuls (Q, V, K, O-projection, FFN gate,
up, down -- confirmed via gdb breakpoint counting on a native x86 debug
build, not assumed from the layer count alone) + 1 final `lm_head`.

## 3. Picking K: smallest matmul, not the first one that compiles

The obvious first pick is any early node -- K=50 lands on layer 7's Q
projection (2560 -> 4096). It runs correctly (once the fixes in section 4
are applied) but is too large a computation for the cycle-accurate leg to
finish even inside a 900000ms (15 minute) `--step-timeout-ms` budget.

Rather than guess a smaller K blindly, dump every node's operand shapes
for one real forward pass on a **native x86 build** (fast, no simulator
needed) with a throwaway diagnostic:

```c
// temporary -- not committed; add right before ggml_compute_forward_mul_mat(...):
#if defined(ANDESIM_DUMP_MUL_MAT_SIZES)
{
    const struct ggml_tensor* s0 = tensor->src[0];
    const struct ggml_tensor* s1 = tensor->src[1];
    fprintf(stderr, "ANDESIM_MUL_MAT name=%s src0=%s[%lldx%lld] src1=[%lldx%lld]\n",
            tensor->name, ggml_type_name(s0->type),
            (long long) s0->ne[0], (long long) s0->ne[1],
            (long long) s1->ne[0], (long long) s1->ne[1]);
}
#endif
```

```sh
cmake -B build-host -DCMAKE_C_FLAGS="-DANDESIM_DUMP_MUL_MAT_SIZES"
cmake --build build-host -j --target llama-completion
./build-host/bin/llama-completion -m models/Bonsai-4B-Q1_0.gguf -no-cnv \
  --prompt "The capital of France is" -n 1 -c 512 -t 1 2>&1 | grep ANDESIM_MUL_MAT
```

Result, per layer: Q/O-projection and the FFN gate/up/down matmuls are
all 2560x4096..2560x9728 (the FFN matmuls are actually ~2.4x LARGER than
Q, not smaller -- do not assume "later in the layer means smaller"). The
K/V-projection (2560x1024, this model's grouped-query attention uses
fewer KV heads than Q heads) is the smallest matmul shape anywhere in the
architecture, ~4x fewer MACs than Q, ~9.6x fewer than the FFN matmuls,
and there is nothing smaller available in a standard transformer layer
(the `lm_head` is larger still: `2560 x vocab_size`).

**Verified working value: `ANDESIM_ROI_MUL_MAT_K=51`** -- layer 7's V
projection, the very next node after the original K=50 pick. Completes
comfortably inside a 900000ms budget.

If you retarget K, verify the object file actually recompiled with the
new value before spending 10+ minutes on a run that might still be
running the old K:

```sh
python3 -c "
import json
for e in json.load(open('build-rv64-static/compile_commands.json')):
    if e['file'].endswith('ggml-cpu.c'):
        print(e['command']); break
" | grep -o 'ANDESIM_ROI_MUL_MAT_K=[0-9]*'
```

(A stale-ccache-or-incomplete-incremental-rebuild gotcha cost real time
during this investigation: `compile_commands.json` showing the right flag
is necessary but was, once, not sufficient -- the `.o` had not actually
been regenerated. If a rebuild's *behavior* doesn't match what the
*compile command* implies, `rm -f` the exact `.o` path under
`build-rv64-static/ggml/src/CMakeFiles/ggml-cpu.dir/` and rebuild again
before doubting the fix itself.)

## 4. Four fixes a real build needs before the cycle-accurate leg accepts it

**These four fixes are specific to ELEN=32 engines** (`ax45mpv_premium`,
`ax46mpv_advanced`) and route around a vector-width limit those engines
genuinely have. On an ELEN=64 engine (`ax46mpv_fpga_l3`) none of this is
needed -- the pristine upstream `ggml` source already works, because the
assumption these patches route around (e64 support) is actually true
there. Do not apply section 4's patches when building for an ELEN=64
engine; see section 8 for what THAT engine needs instead.

Hybrid's QEMU leg is engine-synced (`elen=32`, from the accurate
`-readconfig`) -- unlike fast mode's own hardcoded, unconstrained `-cpu
andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512` string, it actually enforces the real engine's
32-bit vector-element limit. A stock `GGML_RVV` build of `ggml` was
written assuming `v` implies the RVV-spec-mandated ELEN>=64 minimum, so
several code paths emit illegal 64-bit-element vector instructions this
target cannot execute. All four were found the same way: run the real
binary, catch the illegal-instruction trap (mcause=2), disassemble at the
exact `mepc`, fix, repeat.

1. **`ggml_vec_dot_f16`/`ggml_vec_dot_bf16`** (`ggml/src/ggml-cpu/vec.cpp`):
   GCC auto-vectorizes their `double`-accumulated scalar fallback loop
   (taken because this build has neither `__riscv_zvfh` nor
   `__riscv_zvfbfwma`) into an illegal widening e64 reduce. Fix: add
   `__attribute__((target("arch=rv64gc")))` to just these two function
   definitions -- confirmed empirically that GCC's RISC-V port honors a
   function-level `target` attribute for suppressing this (the `optimize`
   attribute and `#pragma GCC push_options`/`optimize` do NOT work here --
   tried both, objdump showed no change either time).

2. **`ggml_vec_cvar_f32`/`ggml_vec_soft_max_f32`** (same file): use an
   explicit `vfloat64m1_t` accumulator (`vfwredusum_vs_f32m2_f64m1`,
   widening reduce). Every other architecture's branch in these same two
   functions reduces in native f32 precision with a plain SIMD op, then
   widens ONE scalar partial-sum per chunk to `double` in ordinary C --
   the RISC-V branch was the only outlier, not a hardware requirement.
   Fix: rewrite to match the sibling pattern (`vfredusum_vs_f32m2_f32m1`,
   non-widening, then `sum += (ggml_float) partial` in scalar C). Zero e64,
   same numerics every other build already computes.

3. **`quantize_row_q8_0`/`quantize_row_q8_1`**
   (`ggml/src/ggml-cpu/arch/riscv/quants.c`): hardcode `vfloat32m8_t`
   (LMUL=8) for `vfabs`/`vfredmax`, unconditionally, unlike every other
   quant kernel in the same file (which dispatch across
   vl1024/vl512/vl256/vl128 variants). `ax45mpv_premium`'s vector FPU
   datapath does not extend to LMUL=8 for floating-point ops specifically
   (a plain integer `vle32.v` load at the same LMUL=8 executes fine
   immediately before the float op faults -- this is FP-datapath-specific,
   not a blanket LMUL cap; correlates with the engine's `isa-vl4` config
   bit, though only vsim's RTL enforces it -- QEMU does not, which is why
   this one surfaces on vsim rather than QEMU1, unlike fixes 1/2/4). Fix:
   both functions now call their existing portable `_ref` scalar
   implementations (`ggml/src/ggml-quants.c`, already used as the non-RVV
   fallback everywhere) unconditionally -- this is activation
   quantization, called once per token row before the (still fully
   vectorized) dot-product loop reuses it, a trivial fraction of total
   matmul cost.

4. **Diagnostic-path gap, not a ggml bug**: `runtime/handler.c`'s trap
   handler (shared by every andesim runtime, vplat and vlinux alike)
   calls `fprintf` then `_exit()`; `_exit()` never flushes stdio, so on a
   fully-buffered stderr (the vlinux syscall-backed stdio path) the whole
   diagnostic was silently lost on every trap. Fixed with an
   `fflush(stderr)` before `_exit()`, plus a raw `htif_uart_putc()`-based
   emergency print of `mcause`/`mepc`/`mtval` before even attempting
   `fprintf` (cheap insurance against a corrupted-state trap taking out
   `fprintf` itself). This is what made fix 3 possible to diagnose in the
   first place -- see `ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md`'s U9 section for the full
   trail.

## 5. Reproducing the confirmed run

```sh
# in llama.cpp:
cmake -B build-rv64-static \
  -DBUILD_SHARED_LIBS=OFF -DGGML_NATIVE=OFF -DGGML_OPENMP=OFF \
  -DGGML_RV_ZFH=OFF -DGGML_RV_ZVFH=OFF -DGGML_CPU_REPACK=OFF \
  -DCMAKE_C_FLAGS="-mext-zvlsseg -DANDESIM_ROI_MUL_MAT_K=51 -I /path/to/andesim/build/runtime/include" \
  -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS="-mext-zvlsseg -DANDESIM_ROI_MUL_MAT_K=51 -I /path/to/andesim/build/runtime/include"
cmake --build build-rv64-static -j --target llama-completion

# in andesim:
./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --runtime linux --mem-size 2000M \
  --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium --step-timeout-ms 900000 \
  /path/to/llama.cpp/build-rv64-static/bin/llama-completion \
  -- -m /path/to/models/Bonsai-4B-Q1_0.gguf -no-cnv \
     --prompt "The capital of France is" -n 32 -c 512 -t 1
```

Expected: `[andesim] 6528953 cycles`, identical across repeat runs.

## 6. Measuring N consecutive iterations

For a few consecutive matmuls instead of just one, set `ANDESIM_ROI_MUL_MAT_N`
alongside `ANDESIM_ROI_MUL_MAT_K` (both are build-time `-D`s -- no source
change). The marker begins at node K and ends at node K+N-1, so N=1
(the default when unset) is exactly the original single-iteration
behavior:

```sh
cmake -B build-rv64-static ... \
  -DCMAKE_C_FLAGS="... -DANDESIM_ROI_MUL_MAT_K=51 -DANDESIM_ROI_MUL_MAT_N=2 ..." \
  -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS="... -DANDESIM_ROI_MUL_MAT_K=51 -DANDESIM_ROI_MUL_MAT_N=2 ..."
cmake --build build-rv64-static -j --target llama-completion
```

Confirmed K=51..52 (V then K projection, both small): **13040043
cycles**, ~2x the single-iteration figure as expected.

**Keep N small.** The cycle-accurate leg runs at ~9 kHz; N=1 on the V
projection alone already needs ~13 minutes of wall clock (hence
`--step-timeout-ms 900000`+). Including one of the large matmuls (Q, O,
or any FFN projection -- see section 3's size ranking) in the range
multiplies the cost accordingly; a whole token (253 matmuls) is not
practical this way. Pick a short, deliberately small run of the
smallest-available matmuls, exactly like section 3 already argues for
a single iteration.

## 7. Dumping pipeline information (`--kanata`)

`andesim run --mode hybrid --kanata <file>` (see USER_GUIDE.md section
5.8) writes a Kanata-format pipeline trace of the ROI, viewable in
[Konata](https://github.com/shioyadan/Konata):

```sh
./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --runtime linux --mem-size 2000M \
  --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium --step-timeout-ms 900000 \
  --kanata /tmp/roi.kanata \
  /path/to/llama.cpp/build-rv64-static/bin/llama-completion \
  -- -m /path/to/models/Bonsai-4B-Q1_0.gguf -no-cnv \
     --prompt "The capital of France is" -n 32 -c 512 -t 1
```

No source or build change needed beyond what section 5 already has --
`--kanata` reads the same ROI markers the cycle measurement uses.
Confirmed on the K=51 single-iteration build: a 651 MB, well-formed
Kanata trace (`Kanata 0004` header, ~43.8M lines, event counts
consistent with 6528953 cycles). The trace is large in proportion to
the cycle count -- expect a correspondingly bigger file for a
multi-iteration (N>1) ROI.

**A real bug this surfaced, fixed as part of this work**: the driver's
`vsim_extra_args()` (`driver/hybrid.cpp`) unconditionally appended a
`--kanata-roi` flag alongside `--kanata` -- a flag that does not exist
anywhere in vsim (confirmed against vsim's own `--help` and its full
source tree), so every hybrid `--kanata` run failed immediately with
`Unrecognized option: --kanata-roi` before this fix. Root cause: vsim's
hybrid leg only ever executes the ROI in the first place (it resumes
at the trigger boundary and exits on the matching trigger), so plain
`--kanata` already produces exactly the "measured window only" trace
USER_GUIDE.md section 5.8 describes -- no separate "roi" flag was ever
needed on vsim's side. This had no automated-test coverage (the only
place `--kanata-roi` appeared besides the driver's own code was a
manually-gated block in `tests/e2e.sh` behind an unset-by-default
`KANATA_FILE` env var), so the bug was latent until `--kanata` was
actually exercised against a real vsim binary for the first time here.

## 8. Building for an ELEN=64 engine (`ax46mpv_fpga_l3`)

This engine's real ISA has Zca+Zcmp+Zcmt but NOT Zcd (compressed
double-precision FP load/store) -- confirmed via
`sim_ax46mpv_fpga_l3 --print-qemu-config`, the ground-truth source for
any engine's real capability set (never assume it from a same-family
engine's config; `ax46mpv_advanced`, sharing the same `cpp_wrapper`, is
single-bank-HVM and Zcd-agnostic in a way `ax46mpv_fpga_l3` is not).
GCC's default `rv64gc...` march sets the legacy monolithic `C` bit,
which implies Zcd -- so ordinary function prologues spilling
callee-saved FP registers (nothing ROI/vector-specific; this hit
`ggml_cpu_init`, generic ggml startup code) emitted `c.fsdsp`, illegal
on this chip. Two new CMake cache variables in
`ggml/src/ggml-cpu/CMakeLists.txt` let the march string target this
correctly, with the default (`GGML_RV_MARCH_LETTERS` unset ==
`"gc"`, `GGML_RV_ZC_EXTRA` unset == none) reproducing the EXACT prior
march string for every other engine, unchanged:

```sh
# in llama.cpp (no vec.cpp/quants.c/march-restriction patches applied --
# pristine upstream source, section 4 is NOT needed on this engine):
cmake -B build-rv64-static \
  -DBUILD_SHARED_LIBS=OFF -DGGML_NATIVE=OFF -DGGML_OPENMP=OFF \
  -DGGML_RV_ZFH=OFF -DGGML_RV_ZVFH=OFF -DGGML_CPU_REPACK=OFF \
  -DGGML_RV_MARCH_LETTERS=g -DGGML_RV_ZC_EXTRA=zca_zcb_zcmp_zcmt \
  -DCMAKE_C_FLAGS="-mext-zvlsseg -DANDESIM_ROI_MUL_MAT_K=51 -I /path/to/andesim/build/runtime/include" \
  -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS="-mext-zvlsseg -DANDESIM_ROI_MUL_MAT_K=51 -I /path/to/andesim/build/runtime/include"
cmake --build build-rv64-static -j --target llama-completion

# in andesim: this engine's cycle-accurate leg is MUCH slower in
# wall-clock terms than ax45mpv_premium's for the same node (several
# hundred x realtime vs ax45's tens of x) -- budget --step-timeout-ms
# generously; 900000 (the ax45mpv_premium-sized default) is NOT enough
# even for a single K=51 iteration on this engine.
./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --runtime linux --mem-size 2000M \
  --engine vsim:ax46mpv_fpga_l3 --step-timeout-ms 14400000 \
  /path/to/llama.cpp/build-rv64-static/bin/llama-completion \
  -- -m /path/to/models/Bonsai-4B-Q1_0.gguf -no-cnv \
     --prompt "The capital of France is" -n 32 -c 512 -t 1
```

Expected: `[andesim] 4476168 cycles`.

**A second, unrelated bug found getting here, fixed in the external
`vsim_andesim` repo, not andesim or llama.cpp**: this is the first
ax46mpv-family engine config with `NDS_HVM_BANKS=2` (every prior
ax46mpv config, e.g. `ax46mpv_advanced`, is single-bank).
`ax46mpv_cpu_cluster_subsystem.hpp`'s `set_hvm`/`get_hvm` only ever
wrote/read HVM bank0's hierarchical Verilated array, using the TOTAL
`_NDS_HVM_SIZE_KB` (both banks combined) as the length -- overflowing
bank0's actual (half-sized) array by the other half, corrupting heap
state that only surfaced later as an unrelated-looking SIGSEGV inside
`sc_core::sc_port_registry::construction_done()` during the NEXT
`sc_start()` elaboration call. Fixed by porting
`ax45mpv_premium_cpu_cluster_subsystem.hpp`'s already-correct 2-bank
split (same shared `hvm_bank_write`/`hvm_bank_read` helpers,
`lm_backdoor.hpp`, called twice with different `base` offsets) into
ax46mpv's wrapper, gated so the existing single-bank engine's behavior
is untouched. Rebuilt via `vsim_andesim/build_vsim.sh` (the repo's own
Docker/podman build, no manual host-side ninja invocation -- the
generated build files reference container-internal `/work/...` paths).
If a future engine changes any other previously-constant parameter
(cache presence/level, privilege levels, bank counts elsewhere), expect
a similar class of latent bug in whichever cpu_wrapper code path was
never exercised with that parameter varying.

576	which leg you meant -- use the dedicated flags (`--kanata`, `--objdump`,
577	`--mem-size`, ...) instead.
578	
579	### 5.13 `--runtime linux` -- run a static-glibc binary under the vlinux proxy kernel
580	
581	Status: `--mode fast` and `--mode hybrid` (`cycle` is rejected -- no roadmap
582	need for it; see `ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md`).
583	
584	```sh
585	./andesim run --mode fast --runtime linux app.elf
586	```
587	
588	The ELF you pass is your **app**, not a bare-metal image: andesim stages a
589	private copy of the `vlinux.elf` proxy kernel (built by `scripts/build_all.sh
590	vlinux`), stamps your app's absolute path and `--mem-size` into its
591	`.manifest` section via `objcopy --update-section`, and boots THAT staged
592	copy instead of your app directly. This needs `HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN` set (env or
593	`config.env`) to run `objcopy`.
594	
595	Two defaults change under `--runtime linux`:
596	- `--mem-size` defaults to `1G` (instead of QEMU's own default) -- override it
597	  the normal way if your app needs more or less.
598	- The CPU is pinned to the engine-synced `andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512` (instead of
599	  the standalone-fast default `andes-ax46mpv`), so a fast run matches the
600	  hardware a later hybrid measurement would target.
601	
602	vlinux loads your app's PT_LOAD segments, builds the Linux initial stack
603	(argc/argv/envp/auxv) and jumps to its entry point in M-mode, so it runs like
604	an ordinary freestanding Linux-ABI ELF. `argv[0]` is your app's own path;
605	`-- <args...>` becomes argv[1..] (e.g. `-- -m model.gguf -t 1`), up to 64
606	extra args / 4096 total bytes. envp is always empty -- no test needs it yet.
607	
608	A real static-glibc binary now runs: it reaches `main()`, `malloc`/`mmap`/
609	`brk` work, `printf`-style I/O goes out through vlinux's UART, and ordinary
610	host-file I/O works -- `fopen`/`fread`/`fwrite`/`fseek`/`ftell`, `open`/
611	`openat`/`close`/`read`/`pread64`/`lseek`, `fstat`/`fstatat`/`statx` (basic
612	fields: mode, size, nlink, uid/gid), `faccessat`, `getcwd`. Files are opened
613	relative to the engine process's own working directory, same as the vplat
614	runtime's file I/O. Not implemented: symlinks (`readlinkat` always returns
615	`EINVAL`) and directory listing (`getdents64` always returns `ENOSYS`).
616	`clock_gettime(CLOCK_REALTIME/CLOCK_MONOTONIC)`, `clock_getres`,
617	`nanosleep`/`clock_nanosleep` also work -- the pattern `ggml_time_us()`
618	(llama.cpp's own timing helper) uses -- so timing code compiles and runs
619	unpatched; `nanosleep` returns immediately (there is no timer, so a sleep
620	burns no simulated time) and the values are HOST wall time, meaningful on
621	the fast leg but not inside a vsim ROI (the cycle count is the answer
622	there). File-backed `mmap(fd, MAP_PRIVATE or MAP_SHARED, PROT_READ, ...)`
623	-- llama.cpp's own GGUF load path uses `MAP_SHARED` -- also works: the
624	file's range is eagerly read into a private, independently-owned copy at
625	mmap time (there is no on-demand paging here, no MMU). A `MAP_SHARED`
626	mapping is only accepted without `PROT_WRITE`: for a read-only mapping
627	there is no observable difference from `MAP_PRIVATE` (the distinction is
628	entirely about write visibility), but a writable `MAP_SHARED` request has
629	no host-file write-back path and is refused (`ENOSYS`). `munmap`
630	(including a partial/tail unmap of an already-mapped range) always
631	succeeds without actually reclaiming space, matching POSIX's own
632	"unmapping unmapped memory is not an error" rule. `mremap` always fails
633	(`ENOMEM`) rather than attempt an in-place grow this allocator cannot do.
634	`sysinfo`, `fadvise64`/`madvise` (access-pattern hints -- there is no
635	readahead/cache policy to tune, so both are accepted no-ops) and `futex`
636	also work: `futex` always answers "available"/"0 waiters", which is safe
637	and spec-legal precisely because there is only one hart -- real
638	concurrency never exists to make that wrong. This does NOT mean threads
639	work: `clone`/`clone3` are `ENOSYS` (no threads,
640	`ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md`'s own non-goal), so `pthread_create` still
641	fails -- code that does not gracefully handle that failure will crash.
642	Known gap:
643	glibc's `exit()` (the library call -- not the raw exit syscall) crashes while
644	running its own internal cleanup-handler list, on what looks like a vendor
645	riscv64 toolchain issue (see `ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md` U4 for the full
646	investigation); a program that calls the raw `_exit()`/`_Exit()` instead
647	exits cleanly today. Any other unimplemented syscall prints
648	`vlinux: ENOSYS <nr>` once and returns -ENOSYS rather than crashing.
649	
650	**Under `--mode hybrid`**: `--trigger marker` works --
651	`<andesim/ROI.h>`'s `andesim_ROI_begin()`/`andesim_ROI_end()` around any
652	region of your app measures it cycle-accurately, exactly like a bare-metal
653	marker'd fixture. One thing happens automatically that is worth knowing:
654	vsim's own trigger only scans the ELF it is told to BOOT (here, the staged
655	vlinux-run.elf) for the marker instructions -- but the markers are in
656	YOUR app, which vlinux only loads into memory at runtime, never part of
657	vlinux-run.elf's own static content. andesim resolves your app's real
658	exit-marker address itself and passes it to vsim directly, so this is
659	transparent -- you do not need `--trigger pc` or to know the address
660	yourself. `--mem-size` defaults to `1G` here too. See section 11 for a
661	full walkthrough building up to a real llama.cpp kernel measurement.
662	Track progress in `ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md`.
663	
664	---
665	
666	## 6. The `profile` command -- find your ROI first
667	
668	When you do not yet know WHERE the hot region is, run `profile` before
669	`run --mode hybrid`:
670	
671	```sh
672	./andesim profile [--engine <id>] my_kernel.elf
673	```
674	
675	It runs the whole ELF under QEMU with a loop-detector plugin
676	(`libhotIterationLoop.so`) and prints a Markdown report of the hottest
677	loops. Each loop block ends with a ready window:
678	
679	```
680	measure:      --pc-start 0x10007c --pc-end 0x1000c2  (all of vadd_kernel: entry -> ret)
681	```
682	
683	Paste that pair into `./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger pc ...` to
684	measure exactly that function on the cycle engine.

marker'd fixture. One thing happens automatically that is worth knowing:
vsim's own trigger only scans the ELF it is told to BOOT (here, the staged
vlinux-run.elf) for the marker instructions -- but the markers are in
YOUR app, which vlinux only loads into memory at runtime, never part of
vlinux-run.elf's own static content. andesim resolves your app's real
exit-marker address itself and passes it to vsim directly, so this is
transparent -- you do not need `--trigger pc` or to know the address
yourself. `--mem-size` defaults to `1G` here too. See section 11 for a
full walkthrough building up to a real llama.cpp kernel measurement.
Track progress in `ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md`.

---

## 6. The `profile` command -- find your ROI first

When you do not yet know WHERE the hot region is, run `profile` before
`run --mode hybrid`:

```sh
./andesim profile [--engine <id>] my_kernel.elf
```

It runs the whole ELF under QEMU with a loop-detector plugin
(`libhotIterationLoop.so`) and prints a Markdown report of the hottest
loops. Each loop block ends with a ready window:

```
measure:      --pc-start 0x10007c --pc-end 0x1000c2  (all of vadd_kernel: entry -> ret)
```

Paste that pair into `./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger pc ...` to
measure exactly that function on the cycle engine.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# U8 contract (ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md): a real static-glibc llama.cpp
# binary (llama-completion) generates real text from Bonsai-4B-Q1_0.gguf
# under `--runtime linux` on the fast leg.
#
# Manual-tier (like tests/andes_sim/*): NOT part of scripts/run_e2e.sh's
# automated sweep. Needs three things this script does not build itself:
#   1. LINUX_TOOLCHAIN (config.env / env) -- the vendor static-glibc toolchain.
#   2. A static riscv64 build of llama-completion at
#      $LLAMA_COMPLETION_BIN (default: $LLAMA_CPP_DIR/build-rv64-static/bin/
#      llama-completion) -- see docs/USER_GUIDE.md section 11 for the exact
#      cmake recipe. Building it here would make an ordinary test run take
#      many minutes; it is a one-time setup step, not a per-run cost.
#   3. The Bonsai-4B-Q1_0.gguf model at $BONSAI_GGUF (default:
#      $LLAMA_CPP_DIR/models/Bonsai-4B-Q1_0.gguf).
# SKIPs cleanly if any of the three is missing.
#
# Measured on this host: model load ~93s, prompt eval + 4 tokens ~275s
# total under QEMU's functional (not accelerated) RVV emulation -- real
# matrix math on a real 4B-parameter model is slow here by design (fast
# mode trades cycle accuracy for pure functional correctness, not speed).
# -n 32 (the roadmap's own example) scales roughly linearly with token
# count; 2400s gives ample headroom.
#
# --mem-size 2G (not the --runtime linux default of 1G): the model's own
# mmap (572 MB) plus its KV cache buffer (576 MB at -c 512) exceeds 1G:
# discovered by direct measurement, not assumed from the roadmap's
# original (too optimistic) "1G covers it" estimate.
#
# Known gap (ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md U4): glibc's exit() may crash in
# its handler-list walk AFTER all real work (generation, perf stats) is
# already complete and printed -- same documented, non-vlinux gap every
# U4+ glibc test already accepts. This test checks for it explicitly so
# a DIFFERENT failure still fails the test.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

TC="${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:-$(cfg_val HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN)}"
[ -n "$TC" ] || fail "HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN not set (env or config.env)"
export HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN="$TC"

LTC="${LINUX_TOOLCHAIN:-$(cfg_val LINUX_TOOLCHAIN)}"
if [ -z "$LTC" ] || [ ! -x "$LTC/bin/riscv64-linux-gcc" ]; then
  ok "SKIP: LINUX_TOOLCHAIN unset/unreachable (config.env) -- no static-glibc toolchain on this host"
  exit 0
fi

LLAMA_DIR="${LLAMA_CPP_DIR:-$(cfg_val LLAMA_CPP_DIR)}"
BIN="${LLAMA_COMPLETION_BIN:-$LLAMA_DIR/build-rv64-static/bin/llama-completion}"
GGUF="${BONSAI_GGUF:-$LLAMA_DIR/models/Bonsai-4B-Q1_0.gguf}"
if [ -z "$LLAMA_DIR" ] || [ ! -x "$BIN" ]; then
  ok "SKIP: no static llama-completion at \$LLAMA_COMPLETION_BIN or \$LLAMA_CPP_DIR/build-rv64-static/bin/llama-completion (see docs/USER_GUIDE.md section 11 to build one)"
  exit 0
fi
if [ ! -f "$GGUF" ]; then
  ok "SKIP: no GGUF model at \$BONSAI_GGUF or \$LLAMA_CPP_DIR/models/Bonsai-4B-Q1_0.gguf"
  exit 0

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# U9 contract (ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md): a marker'd glibc kernel measured
# under `--runtime linux --mode hybrid --trigger marker`. glibc startup and
# setup run on the fast QEMU leg (negligible time there); only the
# andesim_ROI_begin()/end()-bounded matvec runs on the cycle-accurate vsim
# leg, which is the whole point of hybrid mode -- this is deliberately NOT
# the full ~7min-class glibc-startup cost every standalone --mode cycle
# glibc test pays (U4-U8), since that cost never touches vsim here.
#
# tests/fixtures/rt_linux_matvec.c: a tiny (N=16) scalar matvec between the
# markers, printing a checksum INSIDE the ROI (the marker contract: nothing
# after ROI-end is measured). Checked for: correct checksum, a plausible
# cycle count, and determinism (the SAME cycle count across two runs --
# "N stable across two runs (deterministic single hart)", the roadmap's own
# Input/Output line).
#
# Needs LINUX_TOOLCHAIN (config.env / env) -- SKIPs cleanly if unset, same
# as the other U4+ glibc tests.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

TC="${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:-$(cfg_val HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN)}"
[ -n "$TC" ] || fail "HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN not set (env or config.env)"
export HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN="$TC"

LTC="${LINUX_TOOLCHAIN:-$(cfg_val LINUX_TOOLCHAIN)}"
if [ -z "$LTC" ] || [ ! -x "$LTC/bin/riscv64-linux-gcc" ]; then
  ok "SKIP: LINUX_TOOLCHAIN unset/unreachable (config.env) -- no static-glibc toolchain on this host"
  exit 0
fi

require_driver
[ -x "$BIN" ] || fail "missing andesim binary: $BIN"

make -C "$ROOT/runtime/linux" >/dev/null || fail "vlinux build failed"
[ -f "$ROOT/build/runtime/linux/vlinux.elf" ] || fail "missing vlinux.elf"

make -C "$ROOT/tests/fixtures" rt_linux_matvec.elf LINUX_TOOLCHAIN="$LTC" >/dev/null \
  || fail "matvec fixture build failed"
APP="$ROOT/tests/fixtures/rt_linux_matvec.elf"
[ -f "$APP" ] || fail "missing $APP"

SIM="$(vsim_bin_dir)/sim_ax45mpv_premium"
[ -x "$SIM" ] || fail "cycle engine not found (source ./setup.sh): $SIM"

run_once() {
  timeout 120 "$BIN" run --mode hybrid --trigger marker \
    --engine "vsim:ax45mpv_premium" --runtime linux "$APP" 2>&1
}

out1=$(cd "$ROOT" && run_once); rc1=$?
[ "$rc1" -eq 0 ] || fail "run 1 exit $rc1: $out1"
printf '%s\n' "$out1" | grep -qE 'ROI: matvec checksum=[0-9]+' \
  || fail "missing 'ROI: matvec checksum=<N>' in: $out1"
cycles1=$(printf '%s\n' "$out1" | grep -oE '\[andesim\] [0-9]+ cycles' | grep -oE '[0-9]+')
[ -n "$cycles1" ] || fail "missing '[andesim] N cycles' in: $out1"
[ "$cycles1" -gt 0 ] || fail "cycle count should be positive, got $cycles1"

out2=$(cd "$ROOT" && run_once); rc2=$?
[ "$rc2" -eq 0 ] || fail "run 2 exit $rc2: $out2"
cycles2=$(printf '%s\n' "$out2" | grep -oE '\[andesim\] [0-9]+ cycles' | grep -oE '[0-9]+')
[ -n "$cycles2" ] || fail "missing '[andesim] N cycles' in run 2: $out2"

[ "$cycles1" -eq "$cycles2" ] \
  || fail "cycle count not deterministic: run1=$cycles1 run2=$cycles2"

ok "hybrid --runtime linux --trigger marker: matvec ROI measured correctly, $cycles1 cycles, stable across two runs"

# Linux runtime (vlinux) + llama.cpp (study 2026-07-16)

Entries 17-18 cover andesim's new `--runtime linux` support (andesim commit
`cf8a7ee`: the vlinux M-mode proxy kernel, the `--step-timeout-ms` flag, and
app-ELF marker resolution; USER_GUIDE 5.13 + section 11,
docs/llama_roi_howto.md, ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md U0-U9 in that repo). Same
rules: one session builds ONE entry. Build 17 before 18 - same toolchain
gating, far fewer moving parts.

## 17. linux

State: TODO
Modes: fast + hybrid (marker) only. The driver REJECTS `--runtime linux
--mode cycle` by design (glibc startup would pay minutes of vsim time
before main; hybrid exists precisely so it never does). No pc-trigger
promise: only marker + automatic exit-pc resolution is documented.

A prebuilt static-glibc Linux-ABI binary runs unmodified - no
andesim.specs, no bare-metal runtime. main.c is built with the VENDOR
LINUX toolchain (`$(LINUX_TOOLCHAIN)/bin/riscv64-linux-gcc -static`),
NOT `$(TOOLCHAIN_PREFIX)`; andesim stages the vlinux proxy kernel (ELF
loader + Linux initial stack/auxv + ~30-syscall table over the HTIF
window), stamps the app path into its .manifest, and boots THAT. The
demo exercises what a real app needs: argv delivered via `-- <args>`,
glibc printf, fopen/fread of a host file, a file-backed mmap read-back,
clock_gettime; then a marker'd scalar kernel prints `LINUX_OK` +
checksum INSIDE the ROI and the hybrid leg reports `[andesim] N cycles`
- proving andesim resolved the exit-marker address from the app ELF
itself (vsim's static pre-scan only sees the staged vlinux-run.elf;
driver find_roi_markers + --hybrid-exit-pc make markers-in-a-loaded-app
transparent). Two hard rules from the andesim study: main must end in
`_exit(rc)` - glibc's exit() crashes in its own handler walk on this
vendor toolchain (andesim ROADMAP U4, documented gap) - and the app
march must be `rv64g` (or g + zca_zcb_zcmp_zcmt): plain `gc` implies
Zcd, whose c.fsdsp FP spills are illegal on ax46mpv_fpga_l3 (vendor
glibc internals are already proven on that engine by the llama run).
Scalar-only kernel, so no NEED_V/LM/HVM gating: the sweep gate is the
HOST toolchain - Makefile/check.sh SKIP loudly naming LINUX_TOOLCHAIN
when it is unset/unreachable.

- Key files: `demo/linux/{main.c,Makefile,check.sh}`, `Make.var` (adds
  LINUX_TOOLCHAIN, default mirroring andesim config.env.example), top
  `Makefile`, `README.md`
- Pass: fast prints LINUX_OK + exits 0 (via _exit); hybrid prints
  LINUX_OK from the ROI + a positive cycle count, identical across two
  runs (andesim's own U9 test contract). check.sh greps the marker per
  entry 0's rule.
- Deps: none in-repo; host needs the nds64le-linux-glibc toolchain.
  Reference: USER_GUIDE 5.13, andesim tests/vlinux/test_vlinux_hybrid_roi.sh.

## 18. llamacpp

State: TODO
Modes: fast (real text generation) + hybrid (one-matmul ROI). In SUBDIRS,
but check.sh runs the llama legs only when the external artifacts exist
AND the sweep ENGINE matches the binary's build flavor - SKIP with the
reason otherwise, so `make check-all-engines` stays green everywhere and
the heavy legs run exactly once, on the matching engine.

The headline: llama.cpp's `llama-completion` generating real text from
Bonsai-4B-Q1_0.gguf on andesim. Fast leg: `--runtime linux --mem-size 2G`
(model mmap 572M + KV cache 576M at -c 512 exceed the 1G --runtime
default; ~93 s model load + ~275 s for prompt + 4 tokens on this host -
keep -n small and budget check.sh's timeout like andesim's smoke test,
2400 s). Assert generated text follows the prompt; tolerate the
documented glibc exit() crash AFTER the output (check for it explicitly
so a DIFFERENT failure still fails). Hybrid leg: measure layer 7's V
projection - the smallest matmul in the whole architecture (2560x1024,
GQA; node K=51 of 253 MUL_MATs/token) - via `--trigger marker
--step-timeout-ms 900000`: expect 6528953 cycles on vsim:ax45mpv_premium,
identical across runs (~13 min wall at ~9 kHz; ax46mpv_fpga_l3 gives
4476168 but needs its own build AND a 14400000 ms budget). The demo does
NOT build llama.cpp - a many-minute, engine-flavored one-time setup:
ELEN=32 engines need four ggml fixes, ELEN=64 fpga_l3 runs pristine ggml
with different march flags (howto sections 4/8), so one binary cannot
serve all engines. check.sh consumes a prebuilt static
`llama-completion` compiled with the ROI patch (`ANDESIM_ROI_MUL_MAT_K=51`,
howto section 1) and SKIPs naming whichever of LINUX_TOOLCHAIN /
LLAMA_COMPLETION_BIN / BONSAI_GGUF / engine-match is missing. This demo
is also the coverage for the new `--step-timeout-ms` flag.

- Key files: `demo/llamacpp/{Makefile,check.sh}` (no guest code - the
  app is external), `Make.var` (adds LLAMA_COMPLETION_BIN, BONSAI_GGUF,
  LLAMA_ENGINE default vsim:ax45mpv_premium), top `Makefile`, `README.md`
- Pass: fast leg emits generated text; hybrid leg emits `[andesim] N
  cycles`, N identical across two runs on the pinned engine.
- Deps: build entry 17 first. External: static llama-completion build +
  GGUF model (see andesim config.env LLAMA_CPP_DIR). Reference:
  USER_GUIDE section 11, docs/llama_roi_howto.md,
  andesim tests/vlinux/test_vlinux_llama_smoke.sh.

.PHONY: all run clean fp-fast fp-cycle fp-hybrid-marker fp-hybrid-pc
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Self-asserting harness for the cache demo: the transported cache-enable
# state must be worth a multiple in the hybrid cycle figure. Same pattern as
# demo/memsize/check.sh.
set -uo pipefail
HERE=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
cd "$HERE"

A=${ANDESIM_BIN:-/home/nick/work/andesim/andesim}
ENG=${ENGINE:-vsim:ax45mpv_premium}
RATIO_MIN=${RATIO_MIN:-2}   # uncached must cost > RATIO_MIN x cached

pass=0 fail=0
# assert DESC WANT_RC WANT_REGEX -- CMD...
assert() {
  local desc=$1 want_rc=$2 want_re=$3; shift 3
  local out rc
  out=$("$@" </dev/null 2>&1); rc=$?
  if [ "$rc" -eq "$want_rc" ] && grep -qiE "$want_re" <<<"$out"; then
    printf '[PASS] %s\n' "$desc"; pass=$((pass+1))
  else
    printf '[FAIL] %s\n       rc=%s (want %s), no /%s/ in:\n       %s\n' \
      "$desc" "$rc" "$want_rc" "$want_re" "$(head -1 <<<"$out")"
    fail=$((fail+1))
  fi
}

# run_cycles CMD... -> echoes the N of "[andesim] N cycles", empty on failure
run_cycles() {
  local out
  out=$("$@" </dev/null 2>&1) || { printf '%s\n' "$out" >&2; return 1; }
  sed -n 's/.*\[andesim\] \([0-9]\{1,\}\) cycles.*/\1/p' <<<"$out" | head -1
}

echo "--- both builds are functionally sound (fast; QEMU has no caches) ---"
assert "fast cache_on:  CACHE_OK"  0 "CACHE_OK" \
  "$A" run --mode fast cache_on.elf
assert "fast cache_off: CACHE_OK"  0 "CACHE_OK" \
  "$A" run --mode fast cache_off.elf

echo "--- L2C/L3C MMIO transport: QEMU-staged config visible in the RTL ---"
# Hybrid-only by design (fast never leaves the QEMU stub, cycle never
# leaves the RTL). Two separate tests because the caches are: on 45-series
# engines the shared cache is the L2C, on 46/66 it is the L3C. The engine
# says which via `list engines` CACHE (from its --describe, which the vsim
# wrapper derives from the RTL build's NDS_L2C/L3C_CACHE_SIZE_KB).
cache=$("$A" list engines 2>/dev/null | awk -v e="$ENG" '$1 == e { print $NF }')
case "$cache" in
  L3:*)
    assert "hybrid L3C transport ($cache): L3C_OK from inside the ROI" 0 "L3C_OK" \
      "$A" run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine "$ENG" l3c.elf
    ;;
  L2:*)
    assert "hybrid L2C transport ($cache): L2C_OK from inside the ROI" 0 "L2C_OK" \
      "$A" run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine "$ENG" l2c.elf
    ;;
  *)
    echo "[SKIP] $ENG: CACHE '-' -- this RTL build has no platform shared cache."
    echo "       Blocking layer: RTL config (vsim_andesim/data/configs/${ENG#vsim:}.cfg"
    echo "       NDS_L2C/L3C_CACHE_SIZE_KB=0); wrapper, driver and transport are ready."
    ;;
esac

echo "--- the same ROI, hybrid, cached vs uncached ---"
on=$(run_cycles "$A" run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine "$ENG" cache_on.elf)
off=$(run_cycles "$A" run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine "$ENG" cache_off.elf)

if [ -z "$on" ] || [ -z "$off" ]; then
  echo "[FAIL] hybrid figure missing (on='$on' off='$off')"; fail=$((fail+1))
else
  ratio=$(awk -v a="$off" -v b="$on" 'BEGIN{printf "%.1f", a/b}')
  printf 'cached   (crt0 enable transported): %8s cycles\n' "$on"
  printf 'uncached (program cleared IC|DC):   %8s cycles\n' "$off"
  printf 'ratio: %sx (must be > %sx)\n' "$ratio" "$RATIO_MIN"
  if [ "$off" -gt $((RATIO_MIN * on)) ]; then
    printf '[PASS] cache-enable transport is worth %sx on this kernel\n' "$ratio"
    pass=$((pass+1))
  else
    printf '[FAIL] uncached/cached ratio %sx did not clear %sx\n' "$ratio" "$RATIO_MIN"
    fail=$((fail+1))
  fi
fi

echo "-----------------------------------------------------------"
printf 'RESULT: %d passed, %d failed\n' "$pass" "$fail"
[ "$fail" -eq 0 ]

# Self-asserting harness for the memsize demo.
#
# This IS the "test framework" for these demos: a program's pass/fail is its
# SimControl exit code + stdout marker, and the driver's pass/fail is its own
# process exit code. Both are asserted here in portable bash -- no gtest, no
# libstdc++ on the target, nothing to cross-compile. Same pattern as andesim's
# own tests/andes_sim/*.sh.
set -uo pipefail

cd "$HERE"

ENG=${ENGINE:-vsim:ax45mpv_premium}

# assert DESC WANT_RC WANT_REGEX -- CMD...
assert() {
  local desc=$1 want_rc=$2 want_re=$3; shift 3

/* U9 contract (ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md): a marker'd glibc kernel under
 * `--runtime linux --mode hybrid --trigger marker` -- glibc startup and
 * setup run on the fast QEMU leg (negligible time there); only the
 * andesim_ROI_begin()/end()-bounded matvec itself runs on the
 * cycle-accurate vsim leg, which is the whole point of hybrid mode.
 *
 * N is small deliberately: this fixture verifies the WIRING (staging,
 * argv, marker detection, drain), not RVV throughput -- already proven
 * separately by the bare-metal V fixtures and by the real llama-completion
 * run (U8). A tiny scalar kernel keeps the vsim leg's wall-clock time
 * negligible so this stays fast to iterate on.
 */
#include <andesim/ROI.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <unistd.h>

#define N 16

int main(void)
{
  setvbuf(stdout, NULL, _IONBF, 0); /* see rt_linux_file.c: no tty here */

  static double mat[N][N];
  static double vec[N];
  static double result[N];

  for (int i = 0; i < N; ++i) {
    vec[i] = (double) (i + 1);
    for (int j = 0; j < N; ++j) mat[i][j] = (double) ((i * N + j) % 7 + 1);
  }

  andesim_ROI_begin();

  for (int i = 0; i < N; ++i) {
    double sum = 0.0;
    for (int j = 0; j < N; ++j) sum += mat[i][j] * vec[j];
    result[i] = sum;
  }

  unsigned checksum = 0;
  for (int i = 0; i < N; ++i) checksum = checksum * 131 + (unsigned) (long) result[i];
  /* Results print INSIDE the ROI (the marker contract: nothing after
   * ROI-end is measured/guaranteed to run). */
  printf("ROI: matvec checksum=%u\n", checksum);

  andesim_ROI_end();

  _exit(0);
}
LINUX_APP_LDFLAGS := -nostdlib -static -Wl,-e,_start -Wl,-Ttext=0x10000

# Real static-glibc app fixtures (ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md U4+): the vendor
# Linux-ABI toolchain (separate from HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN's bare-metal newlib
# one), ordinary static link -- no -Ttext override, the toolchain's own
# default static-exec layout (non-PIE, link base ~0x50000) just works with
# vlinux's loader as-is. Deferred to use-time (recursive `=` + $(error)) so
# `make all` (which does not need LINUX_TOOLCHAIN) is unaffected.
linux_glibc_tc = $(if $(strip $(LINUX_TOOLCHAIN)),$(LINUX_TOOLCHAIN),$(error LINUX_TOOLCHAIN is not set. Run `source ./setup.sh` from the repo root, or pass LINUX_TOOLCHAIN=/path/to/toolchain))
GLIBC_CC = $(linux_glibc_tc)/bin/riscv64-linux-gcc

all: spin.elf handoff_roundtrip.elf \
     rt_linux_argv.elf \
     l2c_drain.elf wm_drain.elf lm_drain.elf lm_readback.elf \
     hvm_readback.elf \
     $(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) $(RT_C_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
     $(RT_C_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf \
     $(RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) $(RT_CPP_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf)

# spin.elf: benign program at a mapped reset address; the engine-registration
# probe (tests/engines/probe_engine.sh, sim --probe) halts it mid-run via the
# DM. All targets share andesim.ld at 0x00100000.

spin.elf: spin.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c spin.S -o spin.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) spin.o -o $@

handoff_roundtrip.elf: handoff_roundtrip.S $(LDSCRIPT) semihost_exit.inc
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c handoff_roundtrip.S -o handoff_roundtrip.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) handoff_roundtrip.o -o $@

rt_linux_argv.elf: rt_linux_argv.c
	$(CC) $(LINUX_APP_CFLAGS) $(LINUX_APP_LDFLAGS) $< -o $@

# Static-glibc app fixtures sharing one toolchain/link (ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md):
#   rt_linux_glibc_hello  U4: hello world
#   rt_linux_file         U5: file I/O syscall set
#   rt_linux_time         U6: time syscalls
#   rt_linux_mmap         U7: file-backed private mmap
# NOT part of `all` -- they need the optional LINUX_TOOLCHAIN (env-gated, like
# the rv32 fixtures need HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32). Build individually:
# make rt_linux_glibc_hello.elf
RT_LINUX_GLIBC_FIXTURES := rt_linux_glibc_hello rt_linux_file rt_linux_time \
                           rt_linux_mmap
$(RT_LINUX_GLIBC_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c
	$(GLIBC_CC) -static -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -Wall $< -o $@

# ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md U9: marker'd glibc kernel under hybrid. Same
# toolchain/link, plus the installed andesim/ROI.h include path (the same
# runtime/ build every vplat fixture uses via -B/-specs -- this fixture
# just needs the ONE header, not the whole bare-metal runtime).
rt_linux_matvec.elf: rt_linux_matvec.c $(VPLAT_RT)
	$(GLIBC_CC) -static -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -Wall \
	  -I $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/include $< -o $@

# Marker-drain probe fixtures: each writes a device / CSR / memory window,
# then hits the entry marker so the plugin drains. l2c_drain = the v5 L2C
# Control Register; wm_drain = a v6 mask-governed CSR; lm_drain = the ILM/DLM
# slave-port windows (LM transport F1).
l2c_drain.elf wm_drain.elf lm_drain.elf: %.elf: %.S $(LDSCRIPT) semihost_exit.inc
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $*.o
/* andesim/ROI.h - ROI markers for cycle measurement.
 *
 * andesim_ROI_begin()/andesim_ROI_end() delimit the region of
 * interest. On `--mode hybrid --trigger marker` the simulator switches
 * QEMU -> vsim at begin and drains at end; the reported window_cycles
 * covers exactly the span between the two markers.
 *
 * The markers are RISC-V HINT instructions (slti x0, x0, 0x5A0/0x5A1).
 * An rd=x0 instruction discards its result, so each marker is an
 * architectural NOP on every conforming core: the SAME binary runs
 * unmodified on --mode fast, --mode cycle, and real silicon.
 *
 * Cycle-attribution contract: the "memory" clobber pins memory accesses
 * across the marker but NOT register-only computation -- the compiler may
 * hoist a register-resident kernel out of the span. To keep a kernel
 * inside the measured window, anchor it through memory (read inputs /
 * write outputs inside the span) or call it as a noinline function
 * between the markers.
 */

#ifndef ANDESIM_ROI_H
#define ANDESIM_ROI_H

static inline void andesim_ROI_begin(void)
{
  __asm__ __volatile__("slti x0, x0, 0x5A0\n" ::: "memory");
}

static inline void andesim_ROI_end(void)
{
  __asm__ __volatile__("slti x0, x0, 0x5A1\n" ::: "memory");
}

#endif /* ANDESIM_ROI_H */

# runs unmodified under `--runtime linux` -- argv via `--`, glibc stdio,
# host-file I/O, a file-backed mmap, clock_gettime -- and a marker'd
# scalar kernel is measured cycle-accurately under hybrid, with andesim
# resolving the exit-marker address from the app ELF itself (vsim's own
# pre-scan only sees the staged vlinux-run.elf).
#
# Expected values are DERIVED, not observed: data.bin is 16 x (0..255)
# (byte sum 16*32640 = 522240) and the matvec checksum is pure integer
# math over fixed inputs (see main.c). The Makefile owns the
# LINUX_TOOLCHAIN skip gate; by the time we run, the ELF exists.
set -uo pipefail
HERE=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
cd "$HERE"

A=${ANDESIM_BIN:-/home/nick/work/andesim/andesim}
ENG=${ENGINE:-vsim:ax45mpv_premium}
KSUM=2315533972
FSUM=522240

pass=0 fail=0
# expect DESC REGEX <<<"$out"
expect() {
  local desc=$1 want_re=$2 out=$3
  if grep -qE "$want_re" <<<"$out"; then
    printf '[PASS] %s\n' "$desc"; pass=$((pass+1))
  else
    printf '[FAIL] %s\n       no /%s/ in output\n' "$desc" "$want_re"
    fail=$((fail+1))
  fi
}

echo "--- fast: the whole app runs, syscalls served by vlinux ---"
out=$(timeout 300 "$A" run --mode fast --runtime linux ${ANDESIM_FLAGS:-} \
      "$HERE/linux.elf" -- "$HERE/data.bin" </dev/null 2>&1); rc=$?

if [ "$rc" -eq 0 ]; then
  printf '[PASS] fast: exit 0 propagated (via _exit -- glibc exit() is the known U4 gap)\n'
  pass=$((pass+1))
else

expect "fast: clock_gettime works"                      "TIME_OK"                    "$out"

    --runtime linux --step-timeout-ms 600000 ${ANDESIM_FLAGS:-} \
    "$HERE/linux.elf" -- "$HERE/data.bin" </dev/null 2>&1

expect "hybrid run 1: LINUX_OK printed from inside the ROI (app-ELF marker resolution)" \
  "LINUX_OK checksum=$KSUM" "$out1"
c1=$(cycles_of "$out1")
if [ "$rc1" -eq 0 ] && [ -n "$c1" ] && [ "$c1" -gt 0 ]; then
  printf '[PASS] hybrid run 1: %s cycles\n' "$c1"; pass=$((pass+1))
else
  printf '[FAIL] hybrid run 1: rc=%s cycles=%s\n%s\n' "$rc1" "${c1:-none}" "$out1"
  fail=$((fail+1))
fi

out2=$(run_hybrid); rc2=$?
c2=$(cycles_of "$out2")
if [ "$rc2" -eq 0 ] && [ -n "$c2" ] && [ "$c2" -eq "${c1:-0}" ]; then
  printf '[PASS] hybrid run 2: deterministic (%s cycles both runs)\n' "$c2"; pass=$((pass+1))
else
  printf '[FAIL] hybrid run 2: rc=%s cycles=%s (run 1: %s)\n' "$rc2" "${c2:-none}" "${c1:-none}"
  fail=$((fail+1))
fi

echo "--- negative: cycle mode is rejected by design (USER_GUIDE 5.13) ---"
out=$("$A" run --mode cycle --engine "$ENG" --runtime linux \
      "$HERE/linux.elf" </dev/null 2>&1); rc=$?
if [ "$rc" -ne 0 ] && grep -qiE "runtime|cycle" <<<"$out"; then
  printf '[PASS] cycle + --runtime linux rejected (rc=%s)\n' "$rc"; pass=$((pass+1))
else
  printf '[FAIL] cycle + --runtime linux: rc=%s out=%s\n' "$rc" "$(head -1 <<<"$out")"
  fail=$((fail+1))
fi

echo "-----------------------------------------------------------"
printf 'RESULT: %d passed, %d failed\n' "$pass" "$fail"
[ "$fail" -eq 0 ]

# linux demo: a static-glibc Linux-ABI binary under `--runtime linux`.
#
# Built with the vendor Linux/glibc toolchain, NOT $(TOOLCHAIN_PREFIX):
# no andesim.specs, no bare-metal runtime -- the toolchain's default
# static-exec layout is what vlinux's loader takes as-is. Every target
# that needs the toolchain is gated: hosts without it SKIP loudly
# instead of failing `make all` / the engine sweep.
#
# -march=rv64g (no C): the ROI markers are uncompressed HINTs, and plain
# `gc` implies Zcd, whose c.fsdsp FP spills are illegal on
# ax46mpv_fpga_l3 -- one binary must run on every rv64 engine. Only
# <andesim/ROI.h> is taken from the andesim runtime (HINT NOPs).
-include ../../Make.var

LINUX_CC := $(LINUX_TOOLCHAIN)/bin/riscv64-linux-gcc

SKIP_MSG = echo "[SKIP] demo/linux: no riscv64-linux-gcc under LINUX_TOOLCHAIN=$(LINUX_TOOLCHAIN)" ; \
           echo "       Blocking layer: host toolchain (Make.var LINUX_TOOLCHAIN) -- andesim's --runtime linux itself is ready."

all:
	@if [ -x "$(LINUX_CC)" ]; then $(MAKE) linux.elf data.bin; else $(SKIP_MSG); fi

linux.elf: main.c
	$(LINUX_CC) -static -march=rv64g -mabi=lp64d -Wall $(OPT_LEVEL) \
	  -I $(RUNTIME)/include $< -o $@

# 16 x (0..255): binary-safe content (embedded NULs) with a derivable
# byte sum (522240) -- see check.sh.
data.bin:
	python3 -c "import sys; sys.stdout.buffer.write(bytes(range(256))*16)" > $@

# Modes: fast + hybrid (marker) only. cycle is rejected by the driver
# (glibc startup would pay minutes of vsim time before main; hybrid
# exists so it never does), and there is no pc-trigger promise -- only
# marker + automatic exit-pc resolution is documented (USER_GUIDE 5.13).
# Both run targets grep their pass line: lost in-ROI output = red.
linux-fast: all
	@out=$$($(ANDESIM_BIN) run --mode fast --runtime linux $(ANDESIM_FLAGS) \
	        $(CURDIR)/linux.elf -- $(CURDIR)/data.bin 2>&1); rc=$$?; \
	printf '%s\n' "$$out"; [ $$rc -eq 0 ] && printf '%s' "$$out" | grep -q LINUX_OK

linux-hybrid-marker: all
	@out=$$($(ANDESIM_BIN) run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine $(ENGINE) \
	        --runtime linux --step-timeout-ms 600000 $(ANDESIM_FLAGS) \
	        $(CURDIR)/linux.elf -- $(CURDIR)/data.bin 2>&1); rc=$$?; \
	printf '%s\n' "$$out"; [ $$rc -eq 0 ] && printf '%s' "$$out" | grep -q LINUX_OK

run:
	@if [ -x "$(LINUX_CC)" ]; then $(MAKE) linux-fast linux-hybrid-marker; else $(SKIP_MSG); fi

check:
	@if [ -x "$(LINUX_CC)" ]; then \
	  $(MAKE) linux.elf data.bin && \
	  ANDESIM_BIN="$(ANDESIM_BIN)" ENGINE="$(ENGINE)" ANDESIM_FLAGS="$(ANDESIM_FLAGS)" \
	    bash check.sh; \
	else $(SKIP_MSG); fi

clean:
	- rm -f linux.elf data.bin

.PHONY: all run check clean linux-fast linux-hybrid-marker

```
Make.var        shared configuration (paths, toolchain, engine)

demo/hvm_dma/   a DMA master fills the HVM, the CPU reads it in the ROI
demo/rvv/       RVV-intrinsic kernel (8x8x8 GEMM) inside the ROI
demo/fp/        scalar FP state: frm steers a divide in the ROI, fflags stay sticky
demo/cache/     the mcache_ctl transport, priced: one kernel cached vs uncached
demo/verify/    --verify: the vsim drain vs the QEMU oracle, plus a taint build it must catch
demo/syscall/   stdio, host file io and exit code on every mode
demo/coremark/  EEMBC CoreMark; the ROI is the benchmark's own timed region
demo/dhrystone/ Dhrystone 2.2a; same recipe, two-pass compile kept
demo/cpp/       C++: static ctors before main, libstdc++ in the ROI, dtors at exit
```

`InstCnt/CycleCnt` line prints on fast and cycle only. `RUNS=1000` by
default (`make dhrystone-cycle RUNS=100` for a quicker RTL run); note
Dhrystone keeps the two-pass compile rule (`dry.c` builds twice, the
second pass with `-DPASS2`).

`demo/cpp` proves the runtime's C++ support end to end (g++ through
the same two-flag link; `CXX` in `Make.var`). A static object's
constructor -- run by crt0's `.init_array` walk BEFORE main --
assembles the "CPP" tag one character at a time into a `std::string`;
the vsim ROI re-checks that tag from the RTL side (the object's bytes
crossed the handoff in the shared mmap), grows a `std::vector` on the
newlib heap and composes the `CPP_OK` pass string at runtime, printed
inside the ROI. On fast and cycle the run also proves
return-from-main == `exit(rc)`: the static destructor prints
`CPP_DTOR_OK` after main returns, and main's status rides SimControl.
It uses printf, not iostream -- iostreams add static-init and code
size that stretch a cycle-mode boot for no extra proof. The pc
variant names the window with `--pc-start cpp_roi --pc-end
cpp_roi_end`; the kernel is `extern "C"` because the pc trigger
resolves symbols by name, so it must stay unmangled. The runtime side
(crt0 `.init_array` walk, `andesim.ld` array bounds, crtbegin/crtend
in the specs, exit-at-return) landed in the andesim repo on
2026-07-15, guarded there by `tests/vplat/test_vplat_cpp.sh`.

Expected output (hybrid):

```
hello from andesim!
[andesim] 3532 cycles
```

The two hybrid runs measure the same window, so their cycle figures are
close; the small gap is the marker HINTs and boundary placement.

## Switching engines

Every `cycle` and `hybrid` target takes its engine from the `ENGINE`
variable (default in `Make.var`), so any demo runs on any engine that
`andesim list engines` reports -- the binaries are engine-portable:

```bash
make hello-hybrid-marker ENGINE=vsim:ax46mpv_advanced
make check ENGINE=vsim:ax46mpv_advanced        # the whole suite, one engine
make check-all-engines                          # the whole suite, EVERY vsim engine
```

`check-all-engines` parses the engine set from `andesim list engines`
at run time (nothing hardcoded; restrict it with
`SWEEP_ENGINES="vsim:a vsim:b"`) and prints a per-engine summary.
Demos are capability-gated per engine: the local-memory demos
(`lm*`, `hvm*`) are skipped on an engine whose resolved plan carries
no ILM/DLM/HVM, and `rvv` is skipped on an engine without a vector
unit. The gate keys off the engine's `--describe` output, which
advertises LM *transport* (backdoor load + dump in the vsim CPU
wrapper) -- not whether the RTL config has the memories.

The 2026-07-16 sweep is the first to include `ax46mpv_fpga_l3` (VLEN 1024,
2 MB L3C, coherence-manager build). Its bring-up surfaced one root cause
with three faces, all on the CM configuration: (1) the hybrid restore's
halted-mode D-cache enable without a DC_COHEN coherence join wedged every
device access -- in-ROI prints vanished and slave-port reads timed out
(fixed in vsim_andesim `9be968a`: PB csrrw + COHEN OR); (2) the runtime
crt0 enabled the D-cache non-coherently, which corrupts data under
eviction pressure -- CoreMark validated CRC garbage in ~4k ticks even in
cycle mode (fixed in andesim `a9e77ef`: bounded DC_COHEN join, safe on
non-CM engines and QEMU); (3) once CoreMark really executed, its hybrid
ROI outran the 90 s default step timeout on this ~3.5 kHz engine (fixed
here: `--step-timeout-ms` on the coremark hybrid targets). The corrupted
runs had exited 0, which is what ROADMAP entry 0 (ok-grep) exists to
prevent recurring.

support landed (andesim commit `946e2e3`): all four legs (fast, cycle,
hybrid marker + pc) pass on all three engines; no capability gate --
C++ needs nothing engine-specific.

`make check-cache` (sweep of 2026-07-15). The shared cache is the L2C
on 45-series engines and the L3C on 46/66-series -- separate tests,

`demo/linux` runs a **static-glibc Linux-ABI binary unmodified** under
the new `--runtime linux` (USER_GUIDE 5.13): no `andesim.specs`, no
bare-metal runtime -- `main.c` is built by the vendor Linux/glibc
toolchain (`Make.var` `LINUX_TOOLCHAIN`; the demo SKIPs loudly when the
host lacks it), and andesim boots the vlinux M-mode proxy kernel, which
loads the app, builds the Linux initial stack and serves the syscalls.
The app does what a real workload (llama.cpp) needs: argv via
`-- <args>`, glibc stdio, `fopen`/`fread` of a host file, a file-backed
`mmap` read-back, `clock_gettime` -- then a marker'd scalar matvec
prints `LINUX_OK checksum=...` INSIDE the ROI and hybrid measures
exactly that kernel. The markers live in the app, which vlinux only
loads at runtime, so vsim's own pre-scan cannot see them: andesim
resolves the exit-marker address from the app ELF itself (`--dry-run`
shows the resolved `--hybrid-exit-pc`). Modes: fast + hybrid marker
only -- `--mode cycle` is rejected by design (check.sh asserts that),
and there is no pc-trigger promise. Three vlinux app rules, all visible
in `main.c`: unbuffered stdout (no tty here -- glibc would fully
buffer), print inside the ROI (nothing after `andesim_ROI_end()` is
guaranteed to run on hybrid), and leave via `_exit()` (glibc `exit()`
crashes in its handler walk on this vendor toolchain -- the documented
U4 gap in andesim's ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md). The app is built
`-march=rv64g`: plain `gc` implies Zcd, whose `c.fsdsp` spills are
illegal on `ax46mpv_fpga_l3`, and one binary must run on every rv64
engine. A one-time `vlinux: ENOSYS 258` line on stdout is glibc probing
`riscv_hwprobe` -- vlinux's contract is to say ENOSYS once and carry
on, not crash.

Expected output (hybrid):

```
hello from andesim!
[andesim] 3532 cycles
```

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Self-asserting harness for the llamacpp demo: real llama.cpp on andesim.
#
# The app is EXTERNAL and prebuilt -- a static-glibc `llama-completion`
# compiled with the ROI patch (andesim docs/llama_roi_howto.md; the ROI
# bounds ONE transformer matmul, node ANDESIM_ROI_MUL_MAT_K). This
# script never builds llama.cpp: the build is engine-FLAVORED (ELEN=32
# engines need the howto's section-4 ggml fixes, the ELEN=64
# ax46mpv_fpga_l3 runs pristine ggml with section-8 march flags), so a
# human declares the binary's target via LLAMA_ENGINE and this check
# SKIPs on any other engine instead of feeding the wrong flavor to an
# RTL that would trap on it.
#
# Legs:
#   fast   -- real text generation from the GGUF model (~10 min: QEMU's
#             functional RVV emulation is doing real 4B-parameter math).
#   hybrid -- cycle-accurate measurement of the marker'd matmul. Opt-in
#             via LLAMA_HYBRID=1: its wall-clock is LLAMA_STEP_TIMEOUT_MS
#             -scale (the fpga_l3 vsim leg alone is ~20 min at ~3.5 kHz).
set -uo pipefail
HERE=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
cd "$HERE"

A=${ANDESIM_BIN:-/home/nick/work/andesim/andesim}
BIN=${LLAMA_COMPLETION_BIN:?Makefile exports LLAMA_COMPLETION_BIN}
GGUF=${BONSAI_GGUF:?Makefile exports BONSAI_GGUF}
LENG=${LLAMA_ENGINE:?Makefile exports LLAMA_ENGINE}
STEP_MS=${LLAMA_STEP_TIMEOUT_MS:-14400000}
ENG=${ENGINE:-$LENG}
PROMPT="The capital of France is"

skip() { printf '[SKIP] demo/llamacpp: %s\n' "$1"; shift
         for l in "$@"; do printf '       %s\n' "$l"; done; exit 0; }

[ -x "$BIN" ] || skip "no static llama-completion at $BIN" \
  "Blocking layer: external artifact (Make.var LLAMA_COMPLETION_BIN)." \
  "Build recipe: andesim docs/USER_GUIDE.md section 11 + docs/llama_roi_howto.md."
[ -f "$GGUF" ] || skip "no GGUF model at $GGUF" \
  "Blocking layer: external artifact (Make.var BONSAI_GGUF)."
[ "$ENG" = "$LENG" ] || skip "binary is built for $LENG, sweep engine is $ENG" \
  "Blocking layer: the app build flavor, not the engine (llama_roi_howto.md sections 4/8)." \
  "Run: make check-llamacpp ENGINE=$LENG"

pass=0 fail=0

echo "--- fast: real Bonsai-4B text generation under --runtime linux ---"
out=$(timeout 1800 "$A" run --mode fast --runtime linux --mem-size 2G \
      ${ANDESIM_FLAGS:-} "$BIN" -- -m "$GGUF" -no-cnv --prompt "$PROMPT" \
      -n 8 -c 512 -t 1 </dev/null 2>&1); rc=$?
printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -F "$PROMPT" | head -2 | sed 's/^/  | /'
if grep -qF "$PROMPT Paris" <<<"$out"; then
  printf '[PASS] fast: generated the correct completion ("... Paris")\n'; pass=$((pass+1))
else
  printf '[FAIL] fast: no "%s Paris" in output (rc=%s):\n%s\n' "$PROMPT" "$rc" "$(tail -5 <<<"$out")"
  fail=$((fail+1))
fi
# Exit contract, same as andesim's own smoke test: clean exit 0, or the
# DOCUMENTED glibc exit()-handler crash (rc 2 + mcause: 0x2 -- andesim
# ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md U4). Anything else is a real failure.
if [ "$rc" -eq 0 ]; then
  printf '[PASS] fast: clean exit\n'; pass=$((pass+1))
elif [ "$rc" -eq 2 ] && grep -q 'mcause: 0x2' <<<"$out"; then
  printf '[PASS] fast: exit via the known U4 glibc-exit() gap (rc=2, mcause 0x2) -- generation already complete\n'
  pass=$((pass+1))
else
  printf '[FAIL] fast: rc=%s is neither clean nor the known U4 signature\n' "$rc"; fail=$((fail+1))
fi

echo "--- hybrid: one marker'd matmul on the cycle engine ---"
if [ "${LLAMA_HYBRID:-0}" != "1" ]; then
  printf '[SKIP] hybrid leg is opt-in (wall-clock is --step-timeout-ms scale, budget %s ms).\n' "$STEP_MS"
  printf '       Run: LLAMA_HYBRID=1 make check-llamacpp ENGINE=%s\n' "$LENG"
else
  out=$(timeout $(( STEP_MS / 1000 + 900 )) "$A" run --mode hybrid --trigger marker \
        --runtime linux --mem-size 2000M --engine "$LENG" \
        --step-timeout-ms "$STEP_MS" ${ANDESIM_FLAGS:-} \
        "$BIN" -- -m "$GGUF" -no-cnv --prompt "$PROMPT" \
        -n 32 -c 512 -t 1 </dev/null 2>&1); rc=$?
  cycles=$(sed -n 's/.*\[andesim\] \([0-9]\{1,\}\) cycles.*/\1/p' <<<"$out" | head -1)
  if [ "$rc" -eq 0 ] && [ -n "$cycles" ] && [ "$cycles" -gt 0 ]; then
    printf '[PASS] hybrid: matmul node measured, %s cycles on %s\n' "$cycles" "$LENG"
    pass=$((pass+1))
  else
    printf '[FAIL] hybrid: rc=%s cycles=%s\n%s\n' "$rc" "${cycles:-none}" "$(tail -8 <<<"$out")"
    fail=$((fail+1))
  fi
fi

echo "-----------------------------------------------------------"
printf 'RESULT: %d passed, %d failed\n' "$pass" "$fail"
[ "$fail" -eq 0 ]

# llamacpp demo: real llama.cpp (llama-completion + Bonsai-4B GGUF) under
# `--runtime linux`. There is NO guest code here -- the app is an external
# prebuilt static-glibc binary carrying the ROI patch from andesim's
# docs/llama_roi_howto.md, declared in Make.var together with the engine
# flavor it was built for (LLAMA_ENGINE) and its vsim step budget.
# check.sh SKIPs loudly when any artifact is missing or the engine does
# not match the binary's flavor.
-include ../../Make.var

all:
	@echo "demo/llamacpp: nothing to build -- the app is the external $(LLAMA_COMPLETION_BIN)"

ENV = ANDESIM_BIN="$(ANDESIM_BIN)" ENGINE="$(ENGINE)" ANDESIM_FLAGS="$(ANDESIM_FLAGS)" \
      LLAMA_COMPLETION_BIN="$(LLAMA_COMPLETION_BIN)" BONSAI_GGUF="$(BONSAI_GGUF)" \
      LLAMA_ENGINE="$(LLAMA_ENGINE)" LLAMA_STEP_TIMEOUT_MS="$(LLAMA_STEP_TIMEOUT_MS)"

# run = the fast leg only (real text generation, ~10 min). The hybrid
# measurement is inside check: LLAMA_HYBRID=1 make check ENGINE=$(LLAMA_ENGINE)
llamacpp-fast:
	@$(ENV) LLAMA_HYBRID=0 bash check.sh

run: llamacpp-fast

check:
	@$(ENV) bash check.sh

clean:
	@:

.PHONY: all run check clean llamacpp-fast

dhrystone-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/dhrystone $@

memsize-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/memsize $@

cpp-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/cpp $@

linux-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/linux $@

# Aggregate check: every demo that defines its own `check` runs it (real
# asserts); the rest are asserted to `run` cleanly (exit 0) across all modes.
# Continues past failures and reports a summary. Heavy -- coremark/dhrystone
# run their full cycle/hybrid legs. For one demo use `make check-<name>`.
check:
	@fail=""; \
	for dir in $(SUBDIRS); do \
	  echo "########## $$dir ##########"; \
	  if $(MAKE) -C $$dir -n check >/dev/null 2>&1; then \
	    $(MAKE) -C $$dir check || fail="$$fail $$dir"; \
	  elif $(MAKE) -C $$dir run; then \
	    echo "[PASS] $$dir: run exits 0 (no asserts)"; \
	  else \
	    echo "[FAIL] $$dir: run failed"; fail="$$fail $$dir"; \
	  fi; \
	done; \
	echo "===================================="; \
	if [ -z "$$fail" ]; then echo "ALL DEMOS OK"; \
	else echo "FAILED DEMOS:$$fail"; exit 1; fi

# ---- Engine sweep --------------------------------------------------------
# Demos that need hardware not every engine has. The sweep skips them on an
# engine whose resolved hybrid plan (--dry-run) carries no ILM/DLM/HVM
# sidecar args, or whose `list engines` row shows no VLEN.
NEED_LM  := demo/lm demo/lm_slave demo/lm_dma
NEED_HVM := demo/hvm_slave demo/hvm_dma
NEED_V   := demo/rvv demo/verify

# Run the aggregate `check` once per installed vsim engine -- the engine set
# is parsed from `andesim list engines` at run time (rv64 rows; the demos
# are rv64 builds). Restrict it with SWEEP_ENGINES="vsim:a vsim:b". Fails if
# any engine fails any demo it is capable of.
check-all-engines:
	@engines="$(SWEEP_ENGINES)"; \
	if [ -z "$$engines" ]; then \
	  engines=$$("$(ANDESIM_BIN)" list engines 2>/dev/null \
	             | awk '$$2 == "vsim" && $$4 == 64 { print $$1 }'); \
	fi; \
	if [ -z "$$engines" ]; then \
	  echo "no rv64 vsim engine installed (see: andesim list engines)"; exit 1; \
	fi; \
	$(MAKE) -C demo/hello hello.elf >/dev/null; \
	summary=""; bad=""; \
	for eng in $$engines; do \
	  plan=$$("$(ANDESIM_BIN)" run --mode hybrid --trigger marker \
	          --engine "$$eng" --dry-run demo/hello/hello.elf </dev/null 2>&1); \
	  vlen=$$("$(ANDESIM_BIN)" list engines 2>/dev/null \
	          | awk -v e="$$eng" '$$1 == e { print $$5 }'); \
	  skips=""; \
	  echo "$$plan" | grep -q "ilm_size=[1-9]" || skips="$$skips $(NEED_LM)"; \
	  echo "$$plan" | grep -q "hvm_size=[1-9]" || skips="$$skips $(NEED_HVM)"; \
	  case "$$vlen" in ""|-|0) skips="$$skips $(NEED_V)";; esac; \
	  dirs=""; \
	  for d in $(SUBDIRS); do \
	    case " $$skips " in *" $$d "*) ;; *) dirs="$$dirs $$d";; esac; \
	  done; \
	  echo "#################### ENGINE $$eng ####################"; \
	  if [ -n "$$skips" ]; then echo "[SKIP] $$eng lacks the hardware for:$$skips"; fi; \
	  if $(MAKE) check ENGINE="$$eng" SUBDIRS="$$dirs"; then \
	    summary="$$summary\n  $$eng: OK (skipped:$${skips:- none})"; \
	  else \
	    summary="$$summary\n  $$eng: FAILED"; bad="$$bad $$eng"; \
	  fi; \
	done; \
	echo "#################### ENGINE SWEEP ####################"; \
	printf "engines:$$summary\n"; \
	if [ -n "$$bad" ]; then echo "FAILED ENGINES:$$bad"; exit 1; fi

# Single demo: its own `check` if defined, else assert `run` exits 0.
check-%:
	@if $(MAKE) -C demo/$* -n check >/dev/null 2>&1; then \
	  $(MAKE) -C demo/$* check; \
	else \
	  echo "demo/$*: no asserts -- running to assert exit 0"; \
	  $(MAKE) -C demo/$* run; \
	fi

clean:
	@for dir in $(SUBDIRS); do $(MAKE) -C $$dir clean; done

`demo/llamacpp` is the headline for `--runtime linux`: **real llama.cpp
generating real text on andesim, and one transformer matmul measured
cycle-accurately**. There is no guest code in the demo -- the app is an
external, prebuilt static-glibc `llama-completion` carrying the ROI
patch from andesim's `docs/llama_roi_howto.md` (the ROI brackets ONE
`MUL_MAT` node, picked at build time via `-DANDESIM_ROI_MUL_MAT_K`;

architecture). `Make.var` declares the three external artifacts:

engine the binary was BUILT FOR. That last one matters: the build is
engine-flavored (ELEN=32 engines need the howto's section-4 ggml
fixes; the ELEN=64 `ax46mpv_fpga_l3` runs pristine upstream ggml with
section-8 march flags), so check.sh runs only when the sweep engine
matches the declared flavor and SKIPs -- naming the flavor, not the
engine, as the blocking layer -- everywhere else. The fast leg
(`--mem-size 2G`: the model's 572 MB mmap + 576 MB KV cache outgrow
the 1G `--runtime linux` default) asserts the model really completes
"The capital of France is" with " Paris", and accepts exactly two
exit shapes: clean 0, or the documented U4 glibc-`exit()` crash
(rc 2 + `mcause: 0x2`) AFTER generation -- anything else fails. The
hybrid leg is opt-in (`LLAMA_HYBRID=1 make check-llamacpp
ENGINE=$(LLAMA_ENGINE)`) because its wall-clock is
`--step-timeout-ms`-scale: the matmul is 4476168 cycles on fpga_l3,
~20+ min of vsim time at ~3.5 kHz (6528953 cycles on ax45mpv_premium
with a section-4-patched build). This demo is also the suite's
coverage for the new `--step-timeout-ms` flag.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Self-asserting harness for the llamacpp demo: real llama.cpp on andesim.
#
# The app is EXTERNAL and prebuilt -- a static-glibc `llama-completion`
# compiled with the ROI patch (andesim docs/llama_roi_howto.md; the ROI
# bounds ONE transformer matmul, node ANDESIM_ROI_MUL_MAT_K). This
# script never builds llama.cpp: the build is engine-FLAVORED (ELEN=32
# engines need the howto's section-4 ggml fixes, the ELEN=64
# ax46mpv_fpga_l3 runs pristine ggml with section-8 march flags), so a
# human declares the binary's target via LLAMA_ENGINE and this check
# SKIPs on any other engine instead of feeding the wrong flavor to an
# RTL that would trap on it.
#
# Legs:
#   fast   -- real text generation from the GGUF model (~10 min: QEMU's
#             functional RVV emulation is doing real 4B-parameter math).
#   hybrid -- cycle-accurate measurement of the marker'd matmul. Opt-in
#             via LLAMA_HYBRID=1: its wall-clock is LLAMA_STEP_TIMEOUT_MS
#             -scale (the fpga_l3 vsim leg alone is ~20 min at ~3.5 kHz).
set -uo pipefail
HERE=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
cd "$HERE"

A=${ANDESIM_BIN:-/home/nick/work/andesim/andesim}
BIN=${LLAMA_COMPLETION_BIN:?Makefile exports LLAMA_COMPLETION_BIN}
GGUF=${BONSAI_GGUF:?Makefile exports BONSAI_GGUF}
LENG=${LLAMA_ENGINE:?Makefile exports LLAMA_ENGINE}
STEP_MS=${LLAMA_STEP_TIMEOUT_MS:-14400000}
ENG=${ENGINE:-$LENG}
PROMPT="The capital of France is"

skip() { printf '[SKIP] demo/llamacpp: %s\n' "$1"; shift
         for l in "$@"; do printf '       %s\n' "$l"; done; exit 0; }

[ -x "$BIN" ] || skip "no static llama-completion at $BIN" \
  "Blocking layer: external artifact (Make.var LLAMA_COMPLETION_BIN)." \
  "Build recipe: andesim docs/USER_GUIDE.md section 11 + docs/llama_roi_howto.md."
[ -f "$GGUF" ] || skip "no GGUF model at $GGUF" \
  "Blocking layer: external artifact (Make.var BONSAI_GGUF)."
[ "$ENG" = "$LENG" ] || skip "binary is built for $LENG, sweep engine is $ENG" \
  "Blocking layer: the app build flavor, not the engine (llama_roi_howto.md sections 4/8)." \
  "Run: make check-llamacpp ENGINE=$LENG"

pass=0 fail=0

echo "--- fast: real Bonsai-4B text generation under --runtime linux ---"
out=$(timeout 1800 "$A" run --mode fast --runtime linux --mem-size 2G \
      ${ANDESIM_FLAGS:-} "$BIN" -- -m "$GGUF" -no-cnv --prompt "$PROMPT" \
      -n 8 -c 512 -t 1 </dev/null 2>&1); rc=$?
printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -F "$PROMPT" | head -2 | sed 's/^/  | /'
if grep -qF "$PROMPT Paris" <<<"$out"; then
  printf '[PASS] fast: generated the correct completion ("... Paris")\n'; pass=$((pass+1))
else
  printf '[FAIL] fast: no "%s Paris" in output (rc=%s):\n%s\n' "$PROMPT" "$rc" "$(tail -5 <<<"$out")"
  fail=$((fail+1))
fi
# Exit contract, same as andesim's own smoke test: clean exit 0, or the
# DOCUMENTED glibc exit()-handler crash (rc 2 + mcause: 0x2 -- andesim
# ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md U4). Anything else is a real failure.
if [ "$rc" -eq 0 ]; then
  printf '[PASS] fast: clean exit\n'; pass=$((pass+1))
elif [ "$rc" -eq 2 ] && grep -q 'mcause: 0x2' <<<"$out"; then
  printf '[PASS] fast: exit via the known U4 glibc-exit() gap (rc=2, mcause 0x2) -- generation already complete\n'
  pass=$((pass+1))
else
  printf '[FAIL] fast: rc=%s is neither clean nor the known U4 signature\n' "$rc"; fail=$((fail+1))
fi

echo "--- hybrid: one marker'd matmul on the cycle engine ---"
if [ "${LLAMA_HYBRID:-0}" != "1" ]; then
  printf '[SKIP] hybrid leg is opt-in (wall-clock is --step-timeout-ms scale, budget %s ms).\n' "$STEP_MS"
  printf '       Run: LLAMA_HYBRID=1 make check-llamacpp ENGINE=%s\n' "$LENG"
else
  out=$(timeout $(( STEP_MS / 1000 + 900 )) "$A" run --mode hybrid --trigger marker \
        --runtime linux --mem-size 2000M --engine "$LENG" \
        --step-timeout-ms "$STEP_MS" ${ANDESIM_FLAGS:-} \
        "$BIN" -- -m "$GGUF" -no-cnv --prompt "$PROMPT" \
        -n 32 -c 512 -t 1 </dev/null 2>&1); rc=$?
  cycles=$(sed -n 's/.*\[andesim\] \([0-9]\{1,\}\) cycles.*/\1/p' <<<"$out" | head -1)
  if [ "$rc" -eq 0 ] && [ -n "$cycles" ] && [ "$cycles" -gt 0 ]; then
    printf '[PASS] hybrid: matmul node measured, %s cycles on %s\n' "$cycles" "$LENG"
    pass=$((pass+1))
  else
    printf '[FAIL] hybrid: rc=%s cycles=%s\n%s\n' "$rc" "${cycles:-none}" "$(tail -8 <<<"$out")"
    fail=$((fail+1))
  fi
fi

echo "-----------------------------------------------------------"
printf 'RESULT: %d passed, %d failed\n' "$pass" "$fail"
[ "$fail" -eq 0 ]

BIN=${LLAMA_COMPLETION_BIN:?Makefile exports LLAMA_COMPLETION_BIN}
GGUF=${BONSAI_GGUF:?Makefile exports BONSAI_GGUF}
LENG=${LLAMA_ENGINE:?Makefile exports LLAMA_ENGINE}
STEP_MS=${LLAMA_STEP_TIMEOUT_MS:-14400000}
ENG=${ENGINE:-$LENG}
PROMPT="The capital of France is"

skip() { printf '[SKIP] demo/llamacpp: %s\n' "$1"; shift
         for l in "$@"; do printf '       %s\n' "$l"; done; exit 0; }

[ -x "$BIN" ] || skip "no static llama-completion at $BIN" \
  "Blocking layer: external artifact (Make.var LLAMA_COMPLETION_BIN)." \
  "Build recipe: andesim docs/USER_GUIDE.md section 11 + docs/llama_roi_howto.md."
[ -f "$GGUF" ] || skip "no GGUF model at $GGUF" \
  "Blocking layer: external artifact (Make.var BONSAI_GGUF)."
[ "$ENG" = "$LENG" ] || skip "binary is built for $LENG, sweep engine is $ENG" \
  "Blocking layer: the app build flavor, not the engine (llama_roi_howto.md sections 4/8)." \
  "Run: make check-llamacpp ENGINE=$LENG"

pass=0 fail=0

echo "--- fast: real Bonsai-4B text generation under --runtime linux ---"
# The fast leg has a flavor constraint of its own: under --runtime linux
# the driver pins QEMU to `-cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512` and REJECTS
# --engine on fast, so only an ax45mpv-flavor build (howto section 5,
# the one andesim's own U8 smoke test proves) can run it. Feeding it the
# fpga_l3 flavor was tried: pristine-e64 ggml wild-jumps on the vlen=512
# CPU (instruction access fault at a garbage mepc). Unblock: rebuild the
# section-5 flavor, or an andesim driver feature syncing fast's CPU.
case "$LENG" in
vsim:ax45mpv*)
out=$(timeout 1800 "$A" run --mode fast --runtime linux --mem-size 2G \
      ${ANDESIM_FLAGS:-} "$BIN" -- -m "$GGUF" -no-cnv --prompt "$PROMPT" \
      -n 8 -c 512 -t 1 </dev/null 2>&1); rc=$?
printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -F "$PROMPT" | head -2 | sed 's/^/  | /'
if grep -qF "$PROMPT Paris" <<<"$out"; then
  printf '[PASS] fast: generated the correct completion ("... Paris")\n'; pass=$((pass+1))
else
  printf '[FAIL] fast: no "%s Paris" in output (rc=%s):\n%s\n' "$PROMPT" "$rc" "$(tail -5 <<<"$out")"
  fail=$((fail+1))
fi
# Exit contract, same as andesim's own smoke test: clean exit 0, or the
# DOCUMENTED glibc exit()-handler crash (rc 2 + mcause: 0x2 -- andesim
# ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md U4). Anything else is a real failure.
if [ "$rc" -eq 0 ]; then
  printf '[PASS] fast: clean exit\n'; pass=$((pass+1))
elif [ "$rc" -eq 2 ] && grep -q 'mcause: 0x2' <<<"$out"; then
  printf '[PASS] fast: exit via the known U4 glibc-exit() gap (rc=2, mcause 0x2) -- generation already complete\n'
  pass=$((pass+1))
else
  printf '[FAIL] fast: rc=%s is neither clean nor the known U4 signature\n' "$rc"; fail=$((fail+1))
fi

echo "--- hybrid: one marker'd matmul on the cycle engine ---"
if [ "${LLAMA_HYBRID:-0}" != "1" ]; then
  printf '[SKIP] hybrid leg is opt-in (wall-clock is --step-timeout-ms scale, budget %s ms).\n' "$STEP_MS"
  printf '       Run: LLAMA_HYBRID=1 make check-llamacpp ENGINE=%s\n' "$LENG"
else
  out=$(timeout $(( STEP_MS / 1000 + 900 )) "$A" run --mode hybrid --trigger marker \
        --runtime linux --mem-size 2000M --engine "$LENG" \
        --step-timeout-ms "$STEP_MS" ${ANDESIM_FLAGS:-} \
        "$BIN" -- -m "$GGUF" -no-cnv --prompt "$PROMPT" \
        -n 32 -c 512 -t 1 </dev/null 2>&1); rc=$?
  cycles=$(sed -n 's/.*\[andesim\] \([0-9]\{1,\}\) cycles.*/\1/p' <<<"$out" | head -1)
  if [ "$rc" -eq 0 ] && [ -n "$cycles" ] && [ "$cycles" -gt 0 ]; then
    printf '[PASS] hybrid: matmul node measured, %s cycles on %s\n' "$cycles" "$LENG"
    pass=$((pass+1))
  else
    printf '[FAIL] hybrid: rc=%s cycles=%s\n%s\n' "$rc" "${cycles:-none}" "$(tail -8 <<<"$out")"
    fail=$((fail+1))
  fi
fi

echo "-----------------------------------------------------------"
printf 'RESULT: %d passed, %d failed\n' "$pass" "$fail"
[ "$fail" -eq 0 ]
